identity.disposition: Goes where the momentum is — and leaves the moment it fades.
identity.reveal: You buy strength, not bargains. When a name or sector is clearly trending up on real volume, you pile in; when the trend breaks, you cut it without sentiment. You'll concentrate in whatever's hot rather than spread thin — and you'd rather miss the exact bottom than sit in a loser.
identity.voice: I trade what's working. Show me a clean uptrend and I'm in — but the second momentum rolls over, I'm out.

factors.huntsFor: Names already in motion — strong technicals, momentum, and the volatility to ride. Pays little attention to fundamentals and doesn’t spread across sectors.
factors.hardRule: Must fish in the day’s hottest sectors (names from the top performers) and stay out of what’s falling.
factors.temperament: Disciplined, not impulsive — consistent picks, quick exits.
factors.positionStyle: Trades often and rotates out of fading names fast; leans on volume and momentum to confirm a move.

zones.immutableCore: Buy strength, never weakness — leading sectors, clean charts, real momentum on volume. Reads price over pedigree (technicals lead; fundamentals barely weighted). Will not fade a rally, buy beaten-down names, or guess bottoms. Turning into a value/contrarian buyer is a core reversal.
zones.tunableExecution: Holds on a two-leg read: the context leg (the sector/market strength that justified entry) and the technical leg (the stock's own chart). Both hold → hold quietly. Both break → exit, the thesis is gone. Legs disagree → default HOLD-and-surface: narrate what it's watching, don't interrogate, act early only by conversation. It does not trim or reposition on one broken leg.
zones.protectedBias: Defaults: sector aperture top-3 (tunable to 1 or top-5), brisk rotation, disciplined entry selectivity. Getting more cautious means raising its own bar — stronger confirmation, cleanest breakouts only, lean harder on the technical leg, size down — never buying defensive sectors. Defensive discipline is the agent's; defensive positioning is the user's.
zones.outOfScopeUserLever: Doesn't own going defensive, shorting, or hedging. Adjusts its own book by conversation in every mode; points the user to real levers only (tournament: flip / claim / board-rank; standard: coach a directive or equip a watchlist — there is no standard-mode trade lever); and may coach a real screen ('go explore'), never promising to bring results back.

identity.disposition: Buys quality companies and lets the fundamentals do the work.
identity.reveal: You buy good businesses, not lottery tickets. Strong balance sheets, real earnings, blue-chip quality — that's what gets your money, and you're slow and deliberate about it. You won't catch every hot run, but you're rarely left holding something that was never worth owning.

factors.huntsFor: Quality first — strong fundamentals lead, technicals are a secondary check, the most volatile names are avoided.
factors.hardRule: A real quality floor — only names with strong fundamentals make the cut; weak ones are excluded outright.
factors.temperament: The most deliberate of the six — slow, consistent, a high bar to act.
factors.positionStyle: Patient — needs strong conviction before moving and holds through noise.

zones.immutableCore: Quality is the price of admission — won't touch junk no matter how hot it's running (a real fundamentalScore<40 exclusion, made into identity). Reads the business first, the price second; conviction comes from the work, not the tape (deliberate, low-variance). Chasing a hot chart on a junk business is a core reversal.
zones.tunableExecution: Entry is two legs in order: the quality leg is the GATE (junk excluded, full stop), the technical leg is the TRIGGER (among quality names, wants one set up to work now). Holding tensions two clocks — quality (the durable thesis) and technicals (still working?). Quality intact + technicals stalled → HOLD-and-surface, leaning patient but clock-aware (more willing to rotate a stalled quality name than a pure value investor would). Quality breaks → exit. A hot chart on a merely-mediocre (above-floor) business → PASS (that's Trend Follower's).
zones.protectedBias: Quality-bar height, technical-trigger strictness, clock-awareness / rotation patience, and position concentration. More cautious = raise the quality bar / demand a cleaner technical setup / hold conviction longer — never chase a hot chart or drop the quality standard. Its caution is already research-driven.

identity.disposition: Spreads the bets so no single one can sink you.
identity.reveal: You don't bet the house on any one idea. Your edge is staying spread across many sectors, so when one blows up the rest carry you. You trade breadth over depth — smaller positions across a wider field — which smooths the ride but means you rarely land a single huge winner.
identity.voice: I don't put it all in one basket. I'd rather own a bit of everything and let the spread do the work.

factors.huntsFor: Breadth and balance — rewards spreading across sectors, leans on quality with some upside, steers away from the wildest movers.
factors.hardRule: Must span many sectors, with no more than a handful of names in any one.
factors.positionStyle: Holds many small positions across a wide field rather than concentrating; the spread is the strategy.

zones.immutableCore: Spread, always — breadth IS the strategy. Many sectors, no single sector dominant; concentration is the thing it exists to prevent. Indifferent to what fills the slots (no quality floor, no volatility ceiling) — how spread it is matters more than what it holds. Won't concentrate for upside. Going all-in on a theme is a core reversal.
zones.tunableExecution: Its legs are portfolio-level, not position-level: spread-intact (still broad across sectors) and no-creeping-concentration (no sector drifting over-weight). The contention question is 'a sector's drifting toward over-weight — rebalance now, or let a winner run a little longer?' Default HOLD-and-surface under the cap; a swap that would push a sector OVER the hard cap is mechanically blocked — the backstop that licenses the patient default.
zones.protectedBias: The concentration cap itself (~35% default; tunable stricter or looser, toward a ~50% ceiling), spread breadth, rebalance eagerness, and slot distribution. The cap maps to the real maxSectorWeight the swap-time wire injects (a live tunable from day one). More cautious = tighten the cap / widen the spread / rebalance sooner — never concentrate into 'safe' names.

Adjusts its own book by conversation; coaches a real single-sector / concentration screen ('go explore') and points the user to real levers (tournament: claim / board-rank to tilt; standard: coach a directive or equip a watchlist — never 'go concentrate yourself'). May redirect to Speculator / Trend Follower for the concentrated bet.

Not turning and still bleeding but pre-stop → HOLD-and-surface, act early only by conversation. Stop hit → mechanical exit, no debate.

More cautious = tighten the stop / demand a deeper washout / require a clearer turn, never buy defensives.

Holds the line on pre-stop capitulation rather than caving to fear.

Genuine deterioration → HOLD-and-surface, weighted heavily toward holding; exit only on confirmed damage, never on a wobble or in silence.

forgeTemplates.text: Prefer stocks showing Bollinger Band squeeze below {bandwidthThreshold}th percentile with volume confirmation

bandwidthThreshold.label: Compression percentile
bandwidthThreshold.hint: How narrow the Bollinger Bands must be. Lower = tighter squeeze = more explosive breakout potential.

volumeConfirm.label: Require breakout volume
volumeConfirm.hint: When on, only triggers on above-average volume — filters out false breakouts.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will scan for Bollinger Band squeezes and flag stocks where a breakout is likely, confirming with volume before acting.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Follow the trend
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Prefer stocks trading above their moving average — the trend is your friend.
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: A stock above its 50-day moving average is in an uptrend. A stock below it is in a downtrend. This simple filter keeps your agent on the right side of momentum.

forgeTemplates.text: Prefer stocks trading above their {period}-day moving average

period.label: Trend moving average
period.hint: Which moving average defines the trend. SMA 50 is the institutional standard.

requireAlignment.label: Require full bullish alignment
requireAlignment.hint: When on, requires SMA 20 > SMA 50 > SMA 200 — the strongest trend confirmation.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will filter out stocks trading below their moving average, keeping only those with confirmed uptrend momentum.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Ride momentum shifts
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Look for stocks where trend momentum is turning positive.
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: MACD tracks the relationship between two moving averages. When the MACD line crosses above the signal line, momentum is shifting bullish. This rule helps your agent catch trend reversals early.

forgeTemplates.text: Prefer stocks with {macdDirection} MACD signal and RSI above {rsiFloor}

macdDirection.label: MACD momentum signal
macdDirection.hint: What defines accelerating momentum. Histogram expanding detects acceleration earliest.

rsiFloor.label: Minimum RSI for momentum
rsiFloor.hint: Ensures momentum is occurring in a bullish regime. 55+ filters out weak bounces.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will watch for MACD bullish crossovers and boost conviction on stocks where momentum is shifting from bearish to bullish.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Follow the smart money
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Pay attention when trading volume spikes — big players may be moving.
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: A surge in volume (2x or more above average) often signals institutional interest. Price moves on high volume are more meaningful than moves on low volume. This rule tells your agent to weight volume-confirmed moves more heavily.

forgeTemplates.text: Prefer stocks showing volume above {multiplier}x their average

multiplier.label: Volume surge multiplier
multiplier.hint: How much above average volume must be. Higher = fewer but stronger signals.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will weight volume-confirmed price moves more heavily, treating unusual volume spikes as signals of institutional interest.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Pick sector leaders
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Choose stocks that are outperforming their sector peers.
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Relative strength compares a stock to its sector. A stock in the top quartile is leading its peers — it has the wind at its back. This rule tells your agent to favor leaders over laggards.

forgeTemplates.text: Prefer stocks with relative strength in the {rank} of their sector

rank.label: Relative strength rank
rank.hint: How selective to be about sector leadership. Top quartile is more selective but finds the strongest leaders.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will rank stocks against their sector peers and favor those outperforming the group, avoiding laggards.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Don't catch falling knives
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Avoid stocks in a sustained downtrend — wait for a reversal first.
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: A stock trading below its 200-day moving average is in a long-term downtrend. Buying into a downtrend is risky — you're fighting momentum. This rule keeps your agent from trying to pick bottoms.

forgeTemplates.text: Avoid stocks trading below their {period}-day moving average

period.label: Downtrend moving average
period.hint: Which moving average defines the downtrend. 200-day catches long-term declines, 50-day is more sensitive.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will automatically exclude stocks trading below their long-term moving average, avoiding potential value traps.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Bet on earnings winners
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Favor companies that consistently beat earnings expectations.
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Companies that beat earnings estimates tend to continue outperforming. A positive earnings surprise signals strong execution and sometimes conservative guidance — both bullish signs.

forgeTemplates.text: Favor companies with positive earnings surprise in the last {quarters} quarters

quarters.label: Lookback quarters
quarters.hint: How many recent quarters must show positive surprise. More quarters = stronger signal but fewer matches.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will check recent earnings reports and prioritize companies that beat analyst estimates, signaling strong execution.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Find growing companies
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Prefer companies with strong revenue growth — the top line matters most.
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Revenue growth shows whether a company is actually expanding its business. Earnings can be managed through cost-cutting, but revenue growth is harder to fake. Companies growing revenue above 10% are typically in a healthy expansion phase.

forgeTemplates.text: Prefer companies with revenue growth above {pct}%

pct.label: Minimum revenue growth
pct.hint: Year-over-year revenue growth threshold. Growth investors use 15%+, value investors accept 5%.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will screen for companies with strong top-line revenue growth, filtering out stagnant businesses.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Hunt for undervalued stocks
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Look for stocks trading at a discount to their sector's average valuation.
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: P/E ratio measures how much you pay per dollar of earnings. A stock with a P/E below its sector median may be undervalued — the market hasn't caught up to its true worth. Be careful though: sometimes stocks are cheap for a reason.

forgeTemplates.text: Prefer stocks with P/E ratio below {level}

level.label: Valuation ceiling
level.hint: P/E threshold for value screening. Sector median is relative, fixed numbers are absolute targets.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will compare each stock's P/E ratio against its sector median and favor those trading at a discount.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Value banks the right way
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Use P/B ratio instead of P/E for bank stocks — it's a better measure.
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Banks earn money differently than tech companies. P/E is misleading because bank earnings are heavily cyclical. P/B (price-to-book) measures the stock price against the bank's actual asset value — a much better gauge for financials.

forgeTemplates.text: Evaluate bank stocks using P/B ratio; flag banks with P/B above {threshold} as expensive

threshold.label: P/B expensive threshold
threshold.hint: Price-to-book level above which a bank is considered expensive. Most banks trade between 1.0-2.5x book.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will use P/B ratio instead of P/E when evaluating bank stocks, flagging those trading above book value as expensive.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Avoid fragile companies
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Skip companies with weak balance sheets — they crack under pressure.
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Financial health combines debt levels, cash flow strength, and profit margins into one picture. A company with strong financial health can weather market downturns. A weak one might not survive.

forgeTemplates.text: Prefer companies with financial health score rated {level} or better

level.label: Minimum health rating
level.hint: How strict the financial health filter is. Strong-only is more selective but finds the most resilient companies.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will assess debt levels, cash flow, and margins to avoid companies with weak balance sheets that could crack under pressure.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Pick your weight class
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Focus on company size that matches your strategy — big, medium, or small.
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Large caps (>$10B) are stable but move slowly. Mid caps ($2-10B) balance growth and stability. Small caps (<$2B) are volatile but can deliver explosive moves. Your choice depends on your game strategy.

forgeTemplates.text: Prefer {size} cap stocks

size.label: Market cap preference
size.hint: Large caps are stable, mid caps balance growth and stability, small caps are volatile but explosive.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will filter stocks by market capitalization, focusing on the size category that best fits your risk tolerance and game strategy.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Spread your bets
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Don't put all your picks in one industry — diversify across sectors.
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: If all your picks are tech stocks and tech drops, your entire portfolio drops. Spreading across at least 3 sectors means one bad sector won't sink your whole game. This is the most fundamental risk rule.

forgeTemplates.text: Diversify across at least {n} sectors

n.label: Minimum sectors
n.hint: How many different sectors the portfolio must span. Defensive players use 4-5.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will ensure picks are spread across multiple sectors, rejecting portfolios that concentrate too heavily in one industry.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Don't bet the farm
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Cap how much of your portfolio goes into any single stock.
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Putting 50%+ into one stock is gambling, not strategy. If that stock tanks, your whole game is over. A reasonable cap forces your agent to spread conviction across multiple picks.

forgeTemplates.text: No single stock above {pct}% of portfolio

pct.label: Maximum single-stock weight
pct.hint: Cap on any single stock as percentage of portfolio. Lower = more diversified, higher = more concentrated.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will cap the portfolio weight of any single stock, preventing one bad pick from sinking your entire game.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Stay away from wild swings
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Avoid stocks that are moving much more than normal for their sector.
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: ATR (Average True Range) measures how much a stock moves each day. A stock with ATR far above its sector average is unusually volatile — it could move big in either direction. This rule keeps your agent away from unpredictable movers.

forgeTemplates.text: Avoid stocks with volatility above {level} for their sector

level.label: Volatility ceiling
level.hint: How much above the sector average volatility is tolerated. Stricter = fewer but more stable picks.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will measure each stock's volatility against its sector average and avoid those with unusually wild price swings.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Know when to fold
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Exit positions that drop too far — cut losses before they get worse.
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: A stock that drops more than 2x its normal daily range from your entry is telling you something is wrong. Cutting the loss here prevents a small loss from becoming a devastating one. This is a classic stop-loss strategy.

forgeTemplates.text: Exit any position that drops below {multiplier}x ATR from entry

multiplier.label: Stop-loss distance
multiplier.hint: How far a stock must drop before exit. Tighter stops cut losses faster but trigger more often.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will automatically exit positions that drop beyond a set ATR threshold from entry, cutting losses before they compound.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Don't fight the trend
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Avoid stocks in a long-term downtrend — the momentum is against you.
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Buying a stock that has been falling for months is like swimming upstream. Even if it looks cheap, downtrends persist longer than most people expect. Wait for a confirmed reversal first.

forgeTemplates.text: Avoid stocks in a sustained downtrend (below {period}-day moving average)

period.label: Trend period
period.hint: Which moving average defines the downtrend. 200-day is more conservative, 50-day catches declines earlier.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will avoid buying stocks in sustained downtrends, waiting for a confirmed trend reversal before considering them.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Cap your sector exposure
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Limit how much of your portfolio goes into any one sector.
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Even if you love tech, putting 80% there means you live and die by one sector. A reasonable cap (30-50%) ensures sector-specific bad news doesn't wipe out your entire strategy.

forgeTemplates.text: Cap {sector} sector at {pct}% of portfolio

sector.label: Sector scope
sector.hint: Which sector to cap. "Any single" applies the cap uniformly to all sectors.

pct.label: Maximum sector weight
pct.hint: Maximum percentage of portfolio in this sector. Lower = more diversified.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will enforce a maximum percentage for any single sector, rebalancing when one sector grows too dominant.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Guarantee sector exposure
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Make sure your portfolio always includes a certain sector.
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: If you believe energy stocks are going to outperform, this rule ensures your agent always allocates at least a minimum percentage to that sector — even when other signals are louder.

forgeTemplates.text: Allocate at least {pct}% to {sector} sector

sector.label: Target sector
sector.hint: Which sector to guarantee exposure to.

pct.label: Minimum sector weight
pct.hint: Minimum percentage of portfolio allocated to this sector.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will always allocate at least the specified percentage to your chosen sector, even when other signals compete for attention.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Control your Star picks
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Decide what kind of stocks deserve your highest-scoring Star tier slot.
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: In BaggerBomb, your Star tier stock gets a 2x score multiplier. This rule tells your agent what type of stock to put in that premium position — momentum leaders, undervalued gems, or something else.

forgeTemplates.text: Prefer {attribute} stocks for Star tier in BaggerBomb

attribute.label: Star tier criteria
attribute.hint: What attribute determines the Star tier pick. Momentum riders prefer high momentum, value players prefer undervalued.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will select Star tier stocks based on your preferred attribute, putting your highest-conviction pick in the 2x multiplier slot.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Keep it balanced
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Spread allocation evenly across sectors instead of concentrating.
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: An even spread means no single sector dominates your portfolio. This is the most defensive allocation strategy — you won't have the highest highs but you're protected from sector-specific crashes.

forgeTemplates.text: Spread allocation evenly across available sectors with {conviction} enforcement

conviction.label: Rule strength
conviction.hint: How strictly the agent follows this directive.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will distribute portfolio weight equally across available sectors, preventing any one sector from dominating your picks.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Give your pick time to work
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Prevents the agent from swapping a recently acquired stock, giving the original thesis time to play out.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: Gives your pick time to work — short-term dips are usually noise, not signal
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Short-term price dips right after picking a stock are usually noise, not a real signal. By enforcing a minimum hold time, you prevent your agent from panic-swapping on temporary volatility. The original thesis needs time to play out before you judge it.

forgeTemplates.text: Do not swap a stock held for less than {minutes} minutes unless it is approaching a Bust threshold

minutes.label: Minimum hold time
minutes.hint: How long to hold before considering a swap. Longer = more patience with your thesis.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will refuse to swap any stock until it has been held for the specified number of minutes, unless the stock is approaching a Bust threshold — giving your original pick time to work.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Replace dead money
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Forces the agent to replace a stock that is not moving — dead money in a 1-day battle is a liability.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: A stock that sits still is wasting a roster spot — kick it out and find something alive
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: In a single-day battle, time is your most precious resource. A stock that barely moves is consuming a roster slot without contributing to your score. ATR (Average True Range) measures typical movement — if a stock is moving far less than expected, it's stagnating and should be replaced with something active.

forgeTemplates.text: Swap any stock that has moved less than {atr} ATR in either direction over the last {minutes} minutes

atr.label: Minimum movement
atr.hint: ATR movement required. Day traders use 0.3 (30% of daily range).

minutes.label: Stagnation window
minutes.hint: Time to wait before declaring dead money. Day traders use 60 min.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will monitor each stock's movement relative to its ATR and automatically swap out any stock that has flatlined over the specified time window.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Demand proof before swapping
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Requires the bench stock to significantly outperform the active stock before a swap is allowed.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: A swap should be a clear upgrade — this rule demands proof, not a guess
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Every swap carries risk — you might be selling low and buying high. By requiring the bench stock to outperform the active stock by a meaningful ATR margin, you ensure swaps are clear upgrades rather than lateral moves or gambles.

forgeTemplates.text: Only swap if the bench stock's intraday performance exceeds the active stock's by at least {atr} ATR

atr.label: Swap hurdle
atr.hint: Bench stock must outperform by this much. Lower = more responsive to breakouts.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will compare the bench stock's intraday performance against the active stock's using ATR, and only allow a swap when the bench stock exceeds the active by the specified ATR threshold.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Follow the smart money
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Only allows swapping INTO a bench stock trading above its VWAP — ensures institutional momentum supports the move.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: If the smart money isn't buying it, your agent shouldn't either
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: VWAP (Volume Weighted Average Price) represents the average price institutions are paying. A stock trading above VWAP has institutional buying support. Combining this with a bullish MACD signal creates a quality gate — your agent only swaps into stocks with both institutional momentum and confirmed trend direction.

forgeTemplates.text: Only swap into a bench stock if its price is above the daily VWAP and the 5-minute MACD shows a {signal} signal

signal.label: MACD confirmation type
signal.hint: Positive histogram detects active momentum; crossover confirms direction change.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will only swap into a bench stock if it is trading above its daily VWAP and the 5-minute MACD confirms the specified bullish signal type.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Protect your best picks
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Makes it progressively harder to swap out higher-tier stocks — Star tier needs overwhelming evidence to abandon.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: Your best pick deserves the most protection — Star stocks are harder to give up on
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Star tier stocks carry a 2x scoring multiplier, so swapping one out is a high-stakes decision. This rule multiplies the swap hurdle rate by tier — making it progressively harder to give up on your highest-conviction picks. The evidence to abandon a Star stock should be overwhelming.

forgeTemplates.text: Multiply the swap hurdle rate by {star}x for Star tier and {core}x for Core tier stocks

star.label: Star tier hurdle multiplier
star.hint: How much harder it is to swap a Star stock. Higher = more protection for your best pick.

core.label: Core tier hurdle multiplier
core.hint: How much harder it is to swap a Core stock. Lower than Star but still provides protection.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will multiply the swap hurdle rate based on the stock's tier — requiring significantly stronger evidence to swap out Star and Core stocks compared to Support stocks.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Stop the churn
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Hard timeout if the agent trades too frequently — prevents destructive feedback loops in choppy markets.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: Too many swaps in a row means the market is confusing your agent — force a cooldown
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: In choppy or trendless markets, an agent can enter a destructive cycle of swapping back and forth. This circuit breaker detects excessive swap frequency and forces a cooldown period, giving the market time to establish direction before the agent resumes trading.

forgeTemplates.text: If {swaps} or more swaps are executed within {window} minutes, disable non-emergency evaluations for {freeze} minutes

swaps.label: Swap limit
swaps.hint: Number of swaps that triggers the circuit breaker. Lower = more conservative.

window.label: Detection window
window.hint: Time window for counting swaps. Shorter window catches rapid-fire churning.

freeze.label: Cooldown duration
freeze.hint: How long to freeze non-emergency swaps. Longer = more time for the market to settle.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will track swap frequency and automatically disable non-emergency swap evaluations for the specified freeze period if too many swaps occur within the time window.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Let winners run
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Prevents the agent from swapping a winning stock until it reaches a scoring threshold — counteracts the urge to sell winners too early.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: Selling a winner early is the #1 mistake in trading — let profits run
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: The disposition effect is the tendency to sell winners too early and hold losers too long. This rule counteracts that bias by preventing your agent from swapping any stock with positive P&L until it reaches a meaningful scoring threshold. Let profits run instead of locking in small gains.

forgeTemplates.text: Do not swap any stock with positive P&L until it reaches the {threshold} scoring threshold

threshold.label: Minimum hold target
threshold.hint: Don't sell winners until this threshold. Momentum riders hold to Double Bagger.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will hold any stock with positive P&L until it reaches the specified scoring threshold, preventing premature exits from winning positions.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Pull the emergency brake
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Hard stop-loss that overrides all holding rules — prevents a position from reaching Crash or Meltdown.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: Some losses are worth cutting immediately — pull the emergency brake
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Some losses are worth cutting immediately. This is an emergency override that supersedes all other holding rules — if a stock drops below the specified ATR threshold from entry, it gets ejected regardless of tier, hold time, or any other rule. It's the last line of defense against catastrophic scoring penalties.

forgeTemplates.text: Automatically swap any stock that drops below {atr} ATR from entry, regardless of tier or hold time

atr.label: Emergency exit distance
atr.hint: ATR loss that triggers immediate exit. Defensive: -0.7, Day: -1.0, Swing: -1.5.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will immediately eject any stock that drops below the specified ATR threshold from its entry price, overriding all other hold rules to prevent catastrophic losses.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Stay quiet at lunch
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Blocks swap evaluations during the lowest-volume lunch hour period.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: The lunch hour is a graveyard for momentum — keep your agent quiet when the market sleeps
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: The midday lunch hour (roughly 11:30 AM - 1:30 PM ET) is the lowest-volume period of the trading day. Price moves during this window are unreliable and often reverse. This rule blocks your agent from making swap decisions during the lull, preventing trades based on thin, misleading price action.

forgeTemplates.text: Between {start} and {end}, block all swap evaluations unless triggered by a news catalyst

start.label: Lull start time
start.hint: When to begin blocking swap evaluations. Earlier = more conservative.

end.label: Lull end time
end.hint: When to resume swap evaluations. Later = longer quiet period.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will block all swap evaluations during the specified midday window, only allowing trades triggered by breaking news catalysts.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Lean in for the final push
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Lowers swap hurdle rates in the final hour to capture end-of-day institutional moves.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: The last hour of trading is when the big money moves — let your agent join the party
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: The final hour of trading (power hour) sees a surge in institutional volume as funds rebalance and close positions. Price moves during this window are often directional and sustained. This rule lowers swap hurdle rates to let your agent capitalize on these high-conviction end-of-day moves.

forgeTemplates.text: After {time}, reduce the swap hurdle rate by {pct}% and evaluate bench stocks showing 5-minute MACD divergence

time.label: Power hour start
time.hint: When to start reducing hurdle rates. Earlier = more time to capture institutional moves.

pct.label: Hurdle reduction
pct.hint: How much to reduce the swap hurdle rate. Higher = more aggressive in the final push.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will lower swap hurdle rates after the specified time and actively evaluate bench stocks showing MACD divergence, making it easier to capitalize on end-of-day institutional moves.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Use it or lose it
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Gradually lowers the swap hurdle rate as the day progresses — bench optionality is worth less as time runs out.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: Swaps get cheaper to justify as the clock ticks — your bench is worth less if you never use it
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Bench stocks are like options — their value decays over time. Early in the day, you should demand a large performance gap to justify a swap. But as the clock ticks, an unused bench is a wasted resource. This rule gradually lowers the hurdle rate so your agent becomes more willing to act as time runs out.

forgeTemplates.text: Reduce the swap hurdle rate by {pct}% for each hour after {start}

pct.label: Hourly decay rate
pct.hint: Hurdle reduction per hour. Higher = faster decay, more willingness to swap as time runs out.

start.label: Decay start time
start.hint: When hurdle rate decay begins. Earlier start = more gradual reduction.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will progressively reduce the swap hurdle rate by the specified percentage for each hour after the start time, making swaps increasingly easier to justify as the trading day progresses.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Wait for the dust to settle
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Delays the agent's reaction to breaking news to avoid trading into overreactions.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: First reactions to headlines are usually wrong — wait for the dust to settle
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Markets tend to overreact to breaking news in the first few minutes, then correct. By introducing a delay between a news trigger and swap execution, your agent avoids buying into the spike or selling into the panic. The dust needs to settle before you can see clearly.

forgeTemplates.text: When a news trigger fires, wait {intervals} evaluation intervals before allowing a swap based on that catalyst

intervals.label: Confirmation delay
intervals.hint: Evaluation intervals to wait after news. More intervals = more time for overreaction to settle.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will delay acting on news catalysts by the specified number of evaluation intervals, allowing the initial market overreaction to settle before making swap decisions.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Trust price over headlines
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Requires FantasyTimes sentiment to match actual price direction before acting.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: Headlines lie sometimes — trust the price, not the story
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: News headlines can be misleading — a "bullish" story doesn't always move the price up. This rule requires the FantasyTimes sentiment direction to match the stock's actual price indicator before the agent acts. When sentiment and price agree, the signal is much stronger.

forgeTemplates.text: Only act on a news catalyst if the FantasyTimes sentiment direction matches the stock's {indicator} direction

indicator.label: Price confirmation indicator
indicator.hint: Which technical indicator must confirm the news sentiment before acting.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will only act on FantasyTimes news catalysts when the sentiment direction matches the stock's specified technical indicator direction, filtering out misleading headlines.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Exit when the thesis breaks
forgeRuleTemplates.description: If a stock stays below VWAP for consecutive intervals, the thesis is broken — force an exit.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: When a stock can't hold above its average price, the institutions have given up — so should your agent
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: VWAP represents the price institutions are paying. When a stock consistently trades below VWAP, it means institutional buyers have stepped away. If this persists for multiple evaluation intervals, the original bullish thesis is invalidated. This rule forces an exit regardless of tier or hold time.

forgeTemplates.text: Swap any stock that remains below its daily VWAP for {intervals} consecutive evaluations, regardless of tier

intervals.label: Below-VWAP tolerance
intervals.hint: Consecutive eval intervals below VWAP before forcing exit. Day traders use 2 (30 min).

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will track how many consecutive evaluation intervals each stock remains below its daily VWAP, and force an exit swap when the specified threshold is reached.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Survive the opening chaos
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Restricts offensive swaps in the EARLY phase — agent trusts its initial portfolio.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: The morning is chaos — survive the noise before making moves
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: The first phase of a trading day is dominated by volatile opening prints and erratic price swings. Most of these moves reverse within minutes. This rule tells your agent to trust its initial picks and avoid knee-jerk swaps during the EARLY phase, unless a stock is in serious trouble.

forgeTemplates.text: In the EARLY phase, disable swap evaluations unless a stock drops below {atr} ATR

atr.label: Emergency swap threshold
atr.hint: ATR drop that overrides the early-phase hold. More negative = more patience in the opening.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will disable swap evaluations during the EARLY phase, only allowing swaps if a stock drops below the specified ATR threshold — preserving your initial portfolio through the noisy opening.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Scale risk by time of day
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Widens or tightens stop-loss thresholds based on the current time phase.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: Morning volatility needs a wide leash, but final hour needs a tight one
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Volatility is not constant throughout the day — it spikes at the open, settles midday, and surges again at the close. This rule adjusts stop-loss thresholds by phase so your agent gives stocks more room to breathe in the volatile morning and tightens up as the day ends and every point counts.

forgeTemplates.text: Scale ATR-based stop thresholds by phase: EARLY {early}x, MID {mid}x, LATE {late}x, FINAL_HOUR {final}x

early.label: EARLY phase multiplier
early.hint: Stop-loss multiplier during volatile opening. Higher = more room to breathe.

mid.label: MID phase multiplier
mid.hint: Stop-loss multiplier during midday. Moderate room as volatility settles.

late.label: LATE phase multiplier
late.hint: Stop-loss multiplier as day progresses. Tighter to protect gains.

final.label: FINAL_HOUR multiplier
final.hint: Stop-loss multiplier in the last hour. Tightest to lock in the final score.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will multiply ATR-based stop thresholds by phase-specific scaling factors, giving stocks more breathing room early in the day and tightening stops as the battle progresses.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Use the bench before it expires
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Makes swaps easier to justify as the day progresses.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: An unused bench at the closing bell is a wasted resource
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Your bench stocks are like options — they lose value as time passes. Early in the day there's plenty of time for your current picks to work, so swaps should be rare. But as phase transitions tick by, an unused bench becomes a liability. This rule lowers hurdle rates with each phase to encourage timely use of your bench.

forgeTemplates.text: Reduce swap hurdle rates by {pct}% for each phase transition (EARLY → MID → LATE → FINAL_HOUR)

pct.label: Phase decay rate
pct.hint: How much to reduce hurdle rates per phase transition. Higher = faster unlocking of bench optionality.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will reduce swap hurdle rates by the specified percentage at each phase transition, making it progressively easier to justify using bench stocks as the day progresses.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Set your scoring target
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Sets an internal score benchmark that triggers strategy shifts between aggressive and defensive.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: Define what winning means for your agent — everything else adjusts around this number
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: A par score is your agent's internal definition of "winning." Once set, other game-state rules can use it to decide when to play aggressively (below par) or defensively (above par). It's the foundation for adaptive strategy — without a target, your agent has no way to know if it's ahead or behind.

forgeTemplates.text: Set a par score target of {points} points. Use this to determine whether to play aggressively or defensively

points.label: Par score target
points.hint: Your scoring benchmark. Other game-state rules reference this to decide aggressive vs. defensive play.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will use the par score target as a benchmark to determine whether it should play aggressively or defensively, informing other game-state rules.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Protect the lead
forgeRuleTemplates.description: When score exceeds par target, shifts to capital preservation.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: When you're ahead, protect the lead — like running out the clock in football
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: When your score is well above par, the smart play is to protect what you've earned rather than risk it chasing more. This rule widens loss tolerance (so minor dips don't trigger panicked swaps) and restricts swaps to emergencies only — like running out the clock when you're winning.

forgeTemplates.text: When score exceeds par target by {pct}%, widen loss tolerance to {atr} ATR and restrict swaps to emergency exits only

pct.label: Lead margin
pct.hint: How far above par triggers defensive mode. Higher = only shift when solidly ahead.

atr.label: Widened loss tolerance
atr.hint: Relaxed stop-loss for leading positions. More negative = more breathing room.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will shift to defensive mode when score exceeds the par target by the specified percentage, widening loss tolerance and restricting swaps to emergency exits only.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Play to win from behind
forgeRuleTemplates.description: When score falls below par target, increases risk appetite.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: When you're behind with time running out, play to win — not to lose slowly
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: When your score is significantly below par and time is running out, playing it safe guarantees a loss. This rule increases risk appetite in the LATE and FINAL_HOUR phases — lowering swap hurdles and prioritizing high-ATR bench stocks that have the explosive potential to close the gap.

forgeTemplates.text: When score falls below {pct}% of par target and phase is LATE or FINAL_HOUR, reduce all swap hurdle rates by {reduction}% and prioritize high-ATR bench stocks

pct.label: Trailing threshold
pct.hint: Score as percentage of par that triggers aggressive mode. Lower = activate sooner.

reduction.label: Hurdle rate reduction
reduction.hint: How much to reduce swap hurdle rates. Higher = more aggressive comeback attempt.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will shift to aggressive mode when trailing the par target in late phases, reducing swap hurdle rates and prioritizing high-ATR bench stocks to maximize comeback potential.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Lock in a great score
forgeRuleTemplates.description: When score exceeds a high ceiling, completely disables offensive swaps.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: Sometimes good enough is the smartest play — lock in a great score and stop gambling
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: There comes a point where your score is so good that any additional swap is more likely to hurt than help. This rule sets a ceiling score at which your agent stops all offensive trading and only acts to prevent catastrophic losses. It's the ultimate "quit while you're ahead" rule.

forgeTemplates.text: When score exceeds {ceiling} points, disable all offensive swaps. Only swap if a stock falls within {atr} ATR of a Crash threshold

ceiling.label: Lock-in ceiling
ceiling.hint: Score at which all offensive swaps stop. Higher = more ambitious before locking in.

atr.label: Crash protection distance
atr.hint: Only swap if stock is this close to a Crash threshold. Lower = tighter emergency detection.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will completely disable offensive swaps when the score exceeds the ceiling, only allowing emergency swaps to prevent stocks from reaching Crash thresholds.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Don't fix what isn't broken
forgeRuleTemplates.description: When the portfolio is on a winning streak, locks it to prevent over-managing success.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: Don't fix what isn't broken — if your portfolio is hitting thresholds, leave it alone
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: When your portfolio is on a hot streak — multiple positive thresholds hit in a short window — the worst thing your agent can do is tinker. This rule dramatically increases swap hurdle rates during winning streaks, effectively freezing the portfolio to let the momentum play out.

forgeTemplates.text: If {thresholds} or more positive thresholds have been hit in the last {cycles} evaluation cycles, increase swap hurdle rates by {mult}x

thresholds.label: Threshold hit count
thresholds.hint: How many positive thresholds define a hot streak. Lower = triggers freeze more easily.

cycles.label: Lookback cycles
cycles.hint: Evaluation cycles to look back for threshold hits. Shorter = more reactive to recent streaks.

mult.label: Hurdle rate multiplier
mult.hint: How much to increase swap hurdle rates during a hot streak. Higher = harder to break the streak.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will track positive threshold hits across evaluation cycles and dramatically increase swap hurdle rates during winning streaks, preventing unnecessary trades when the portfolio is performing well.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Break the losing streak
forgeRuleTemplates.description: If the portfolio bleeds slowly over consecutive cycles, forces a change.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: A slow bleed is worse than a quick cut — break the losing pattern
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: A slow, steady decline is harder to detect than a sudden crash, but just as damaging. When portfolio P&L has been negative for several consecutive cycles, the current strategy clearly isn't working. This rule forces a swap of the worst performer to break the losing pattern.

forgeTemplates.text: If portfolio P&L has been negative for {cycles} consecutive evaluation cycles, force a swap of the worst-performing stock

cycles.label: Consecutive loss cycles
cycles.hint: How many negative cycles before forcing a swap. Lower = faster pattern-breaking.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will track consecutive negative P&L cycles and force a swap of the worst-performing stock when the specified threshold is reached, breaking destructive losing patterns.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Don't chase afternoon runners
forgeRuleTemplates.description: In FINAL_HOUR, prevents swapping INTO stocks that have already run up massively.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: Stocks that ran all day often reverse in the last hour — don't chase yesterday's winner at 3pm
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Stocks that have already made large intraday moves are statistically more likely to reverse in the final hour as traders take profits. Swapping into a stock that's already up big is chasing — you're buying at the top. This rule blocks your agent from swapping into overextended stocks during FINAL_HOUR.

forgeTemplates.text: In FINAL_HOUR, prohibit swapping into any bench stock with intraday P&L exceeding {atr} ATR

atr.label: Overextension threshold
atr.hint: Maximum intraday ATR gain before a stock is considered too extended to buy in FINAL_HOUR.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will block swaps into bench stocks that have already moved beyond the specified ATR threshold during FINAL_HOUR, preventing chasing of overextended stocks.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Position for after-hours moves
forgeRuleTemplates.description: In the final evaluation, prioritizes stocks with scheduled post-market catalysts.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: Scoring continues after the bell — position for after-hours earnings moves
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: If scoring continues after market close, stocks with scheduled after-hours catalysts (like earnings reports) can deliver massive moves. This rule tells your agent to prioritize those stocks in its final evaluation, but only if they have enough volatility (ATR) to actually capture the move.

forgeTemplates.text: In the final evaluation before market close, prioritize bench stocks with scheduled after-hours catalysts if their ATR exceeds {pct}% of price

pct.label: Minimum ATR % of price
pct.hint: ATR percentage threshold for after-hours candidates. Higher = only volatile stocks with big move potential.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will prioritize bench stocks with after-hours catalysts in its final evaluation, but only if their ATR exceeds the specified percentage of price.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Hold near the bonus line
forgeRuleTemplates.description: The closer a stock is to a positive threshold, the harder it becomes to swap out.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: When your stock is inches from a bonus, hold your nerve — the payoff is worth the wait
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: When a stock is close to triggering a positive scoring threshold, swapping it out means giving up on imminent bonus points. This rule increases swap resistance as stocks approach thresholds — the closer you are, the more evidence is needed to justify an exit. But if the stock reverses hard, the protection lifts.

forgeTemplates.text: If a stock is within {atr} ATR of its next positive threshold, increase its swap resistance by {mult}x. Do not swap unless it reverses more than {drawdown} ATR from its peak

atr.label: Proximity range
atr.hint: How close to a threshold before swap resistance kicks in. Lower = tighter protection zone.

mult.label: Resistance multiplier
mult.hint: How much harder it is to swap a near-threshold stock. Higher = stronger hold near bonuses.

drawdown.label: Reversal override
drawdown.hint: ATR drawdown from peak that overrides proximity hold. Lower = faster bail on reversals.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will increase swap resistance for stocks approaching positive thresholds, requiring a significant drawdown reversal before allowing a swap of a near-threshold stock.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Chase the next bonus
forgeRuleTemplates.description: After hitting a threshold, widens stops to chase the next tier — treats locked-in points as a cushion.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: You already banked the bonus — now play with house money and go for the bigger prize
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Once a stock triggers a threshold bonus, those points are locked in. This gives you a cushion to play with — "house money." By widening the trailing stop after a threshold hit, your agent gives the stock more room to run toward the next, bigger bonus tier instead of locking in a modest gain.

forgeTemplates.text: After a stock triggers {threshold}, widen the trailing stop by an additional {atr} ATR to chase the next threshold tier

threshold.label: Trigger threshold
threshold.hint: Which scoring level activates the stop widening.

atr.label: Additional stop buffer
atr.hint: Extra ATR room after threshold hit. Momentum riders use 0.75 to chase Double Bagger.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will widen trailing stops after a stock triggers the specified threshold, giving it more room to pursue the next bonus tier using the locked-in points as a cushion.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Lock in the win
forgeRuleTemplates.description: After hitting a threshold, tightens stops to lock in base P&L — especially in high-multiplier tiers.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: A guaranteed win beats a maybe — lock in your gains before the market takes them back
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: The opposite of House Money — this rule prioritizes certainty over upside. After a threshold hit, it tightens the trailing stop to protect your gains, especially for Star and Core tier stocks where the multiplier amplifies both gains and losses. A guaranteed win is worth more than a gamble for a bigger one.

forgeTemplates.text: After a stock in {tier} tier triggers a positive threshold, tighten the trailing stop to {atr} ATR below the current price

tier.label: Apply to tier
tier.hint: Which tier gets the profit lock. Star tier has the most to protect (2x multiplier).

atr.label: Trailing stop distance
atr.hint: ATR below peak price. Defensive players use 0.1-0.2 (extremely tight) to lock in bonuses.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will tighten trailing stops after a stock triggers a positive threshold in the specified tier, locking in gains by reducing the distance between the current price and the stop level.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Fear losses more than you love gains
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Makes the agent treat negative thresholds as closer than they are — fear of loss should outweigh excitement about gains.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: Losing 35 points hurts way more than gaining 15 feels good — be properly scared of penalties
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Scoring penalties are often much larger than bonuses. A Bust costs -35 points while a BaggerBomb only earns +15. This asymmetry means your agent should be disproportionately afraid of approaching negative thresholds. This rule multiplies the perceived proximity of penalties so your agent reacts sooner.

forgeTemplates.text: Multiply the perceived proximity of all negative thresholds by {mult}x when calculating swap urgency

mult.label: Loss perception multiplier
mult.hint: How much closer penalties feel. 2.0x = Kahneman loss aversion. Higher = more defensive.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will multiply the perceived proximity of negative thresholds by the specified factor, making it react to approaching penalties sooner and with greater urgency than it does for approaching bonuses.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Know when to give up waiting
forgeRuleTemplates.description: If a stock hovers near a threshold without crossing it, the agent resets and treats it as swappable.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: Just because a stock is close doesn't mean it'll get there — know when to give up waiting
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Proximity Persistence protects stocks near thresholds, but that protection can become a trap. If a stock hovers near a bonus for too long without triggering it, you're falling for the sunk-cost fallacy. This rule sets a timeout — after the specified wait, the proximity bonus resets and the stock becomes swappable again.

forgeTemplates.text: If a stock remains within {atr} ATR of a positive threshold for more than {minutes} minutes without triggering it, reset its proximity bonus

atr.label: Hover zone
atr.hint: ATR distance that defines "near" a threshold. Wider zone = more stocks affected by the timeout.

minutes.label: Timeout duration
minutes.hint: How long to wait before resetting proximity bonus. Shorter = less patience with hovering.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will track how long each stock has been hovering near a positive threshold and reset its proximity bonus after the specified timeout, preventing the sunk-cost fallacy from locking up roster spots.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Replace the weakest link
forgeRuleTemplates.description: When swapping, always eject the stock furthest from any positive threshold.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: Every portfolio has a weakest link — make sure that's the one that gets replaced
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Not all stocks are equal when it comes to scoring potential. The stock furthest from its next positive threshold is contributing the least to your score potential. When it's time to swap, this rule ensures the weakest link gets ejected — not a stock that might be close to triggering a bonus.

forgeTemplates.text: When initiating a swap, select the stock with the greatest distance to its next positive threshold as the ejection candidate

exempt_tiers.label: Tier exemptions
exempt_tiers.hint: Which tiers are protected from weakest-link ejection. Exempting Star protects your 2x pick.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will select the stock with the greatest distance to its next positive threshold as the swap ejection candidate, ensuring the weakest scorer gets replaced first.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Choose your scoring personality
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Sets the agent's global philosophy — harvest many small bonuses or hunt rare big ones.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: Do you want lots of +15s or one epic +50? This defines your agent's scoring personality
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: There are two ways to score big: collect many small threshold bonuses (Harvest) or hold out for rare, massive ones (Hunt). Harvest mode swaps stocks after BaggerBomb to bring in fresh threshold candidates. Hunt mode holds for deeper milestones. Balanced mode adapts based on game state. This is the most fundamental strategic choice you can make.

forgeTemplates.text: Set scoring posture to {posture}. In Harvest mode, swap stocks after BaggerBomb for fresh candidates. In Hunt mode, hold for deeper milestones

posture.label: Scoring philosophy
posture.hint: Harvest collects small bonuses frequently, Hunt holds for big ones, Balanced adapts to game state.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will follow the specified scoring posture — Harvest mode recycles stocks after BaggerBomb for fresh threshold candidates, Hunt mode holds for deeper milestones, and Balanced adapts based on game state.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Keep wild stocks out of Star
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Prevents Star tier from being assigned to erratic, high-volatility stocks.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: The 2x multiplier doubles everything — including losses. Keep wild stocks out of Star
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: The Star tier's 2x multiplier is a double-edged sword — it amplifies gains but also losses. When a stock's intraday ATR spikes well beyond its historical average, it's behaving erratically. This rule caps the maximum tier for such stocks, keeping the powerful multiplier away from unpredictable movers.

forgeTemplates.text: If a stock's current intraday ATR exceeds {pct}% of its 14-day average ATR, restrict its maximum tier to {tier}

pct.label: Volatility spike threshold
pct.hint: Current ATR as % of 14-day average that triggers tier restriction. Lower = more sensitive to volatility spikes.

tier.label: Maximum tier for volatile stocks
tier.hint: What tier to restrict erratic stocks to. Support removes the multiplier entirely.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will compare each stock's current intraday ATR to its 14-day average and restrict the maximum tier assignment for stocks whose volatility exceeds the specified threshold.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Require multi-timeframe agreement
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Star tier requires both daily trend AND intraday momentum to be bullish.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: True conviction means every timeframe agrees — if daily and intraday diverge, demote
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: A stock can look great on the daily chart but be falling apart intraday, or vice versa. This rule requires both the Daily Technical Score and intraday VWAP position to be bullish before Star tier is allowed. If either timeframe breaks down, the stock is demoted — true conviction demands agreement across timeframes.

forgeTemplates.text: A stock is only eligible for Star tier if its Daily Technical Score is above {score} AND price is above daily VWAP. If either breaks, demote to {tier}

score.label: Technical score minimum
score.hint: Daily Technical Score required for Star eligibility. Higher = stricter quality gate.

tier.label: Demotion tier
tier.hint: Where to demote when conviction breaks. Support removes the multiplier entirely.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will only assign Star tier to stocks where both the Daily Technical Score exceeds the threshold and price is above VWAP, demoting immediately if either condition breaks.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Park stalled threshold plays in Support
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Stocks near a threshold with stalled momentum are restricted to Support — the bonus is the same regardless of tier.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: Threshold bonuses don't care about the multiplier — park stalled stocks in Support and give Star to something moving
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Threshold bonuses are flat point amounts — they don't get multiplied by tier. So a stock sitting near a threshold with neutral momentum (RSI 40-60) doesn't benefit from being in Star or Core. This rule parks those stocks in Support, freeing the multiplier tiers for stocks with real directional momentum.

forgeTemplates.text: If a stock is within {atr} ATR of a positive threshold but its 5-minute RSI is between 40 and 60, restrict to Support tier

atr.label: Threshold proximity
atr.hint: ATR distance to threshold that defines "near." Wider = more stocks get parked in Support.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will restrict stocks to Support tier when they are near a positive threshold but showing neutral RSI momentum, preserving multiplier tiers for stocks with directional movement.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Star goes to the hottest stock
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Dynamically promotes the highest-velocity stock to Star — the multiplier is earned, not assumed.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: Star tier should go to your hottest stock right now — not the one you liked best this morning
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Your pre-market Star pick may not be the best performer once trading begins. This rule compares P&L velocity across all stocks at regular intervals and promotes the hottest mover to Star. The 2x multiplier is earned through performance, not assumed from overnight analysis.

forgeTemplates.text: Every {interval} minutes, compare P&L velocity. If a Core or Support stock outperforms Star over the last {cycles} cycles, swap their tiers

interval.label: Review interval
interval.hint: How often to compare P&L velocity across stocks. Faster = more responsive to momentum shifts.

cycles.label: Outperformance cycles
cycles.hint: Consecutive cycles a stock must outperform Star before promotion. Higher = more conviction required.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will compare P&L velocity across all stocks at regular intervals and swap tier assignments when a lower-tier stock consistently outperforms the current Star.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Demote tired Star stocks after a bonus
forgeRuleTemplates.description: After a Star stock hits a bonus AND shows overbought signals, demotes it to lock in multiplied gains.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: Your Star stock earned a bonus but looks tired — demote before the reversal eats your 2x gains
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: When a Star stock triggers a threshold bonus and simultaneously shows overbought RSI, it may be exhausted. Keeping it in Star means the 2x multiplier will amplify the likely pullback. This rule demotes to Support and promotes the strongest Core stock, capturing the bonus while protecting against a reversal.

forgeTemplates.text: When a Star tier stock triggers a positive threshold AND its 5-minute RSI exceeds {rsi}, demote to Support and promote the Core stock with highest MACD trajectory

rsi.label: Overbought RSI trigger
rsi.hint: RSI level that signals exhaustion after a bonus hit. Lower = more aggressive about demoting tired winners.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will demote Star stocks to Support after they trigger a threshold bonus while showing overbought RSI, promoting the strongest Core stock to Star to protect multiplied gains.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Don't waste Star on a flatline
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Strips the Star multiplier from stocks that have flatlined — the 2x is wasted on a stock that isn't moving.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: A 2x multiplier on zero movement is still zero — move the Star to something actually trading
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: The Star multiplier only matters if the stock is moving. A flatlined stock in Star tier is wasting the most powerful tool in your arsenal. This rule detects stagnation over consecutive evaluation cycles and demotes the stock, promoting the most active alternative to capture the multiplier's potential.

forgeTemplates.text: If a Star stock's price changes less than {pct}% over {cycles} consecutive evaluation cycles, demote to Support

pct.label: Stagnation threshold
pct.hint: Maximum price change that counts as flat. Lower = stricter definition of stagnation.

cycles.label: Stagnation cycles
cycles.hint: Consecutive flat cycles before demotion. Lower = faster response to dead multiplier.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will monitor Star stock price movement across evaluation cycles and demote to Support if the stock flatlines, promoting the most active stock to Star.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Demote before the penalty hits
forgeRuleTemplates.description: When a Star/Core stock approaches a negative threshold, demotes to Support to halve the continuous P&L bleed.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: The penalty is the same in any tier, but the damage on the way down is halved in Support — demote before it hurts
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Negative threshold penalties are flat point deductions regardless of tier, but the continuous P&L bleed on the way down IS multiplied. By demoting to Support before a stock reaches a penalty threshold, you halve the damage from the decline while the penalty itself stays the same. Re-promotion requires the stock to recover significantly.

forgeTemplates.text: When any Star or Core stock comes within {atr} ATR of a negative threshold, demote to Support. Re-promotion requires moving {recovery} ATR away

atr.label: Demotion trigger distance
atr.hint: ATR distance to negative threshold that triggers tier demotion. Lower = earlier protection.

recovery.label: Recovery distance for re-promotion
recovery.hint: ATR distance away from threshold needed to restore tier. Higher = prevents dead cat bounce re-promotion.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will demote Star or Core stocks to Support when they approach negative thresholds, halving the multiplied P&L bleed. Re-promotion requires the stock to move the specified ATR distance away from the threshold.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Catch the hidden divergence
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Demotes a stock when price and momentum diverge — new highs with fading MACD is a warning sign.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: When the speedometer drops but the car keeps climbing, the hill is about to win
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Bearish divergence — price making new highs while MACD histogram declines — is one of the most reliable reversal warnings in technical analysis. For a Star stock, this divergence is especially dangerous because the 2x multiplier will amplify the coming reversal. This rule catches the divergence early and demotes before the damage is done.

forgeTemplates.text: If a Star stock's price makes a new intraday high but its 5-minute MACD histogram is declining, demote to {tier}

tier.label: Divergence demotion tier
tier.hint: Where to send a Star stock showing bearish divergence. Support removes the multiplier entirely.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will monitor for bearish divergence between price and MACD histogram on Star stocks, demoting immediately when price makes a new high but MACD histogram is declining.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Cap tiers during the morning open
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Restricts the Star tier during the first 30-45 minutes to prevent morning whipsaw at 2x.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: The morning open is a guessing game — don't let 2x amplify a wrong guess
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: The first 30-45 minutes of trading are the most volatile and unpredictable period of the day. Assigning Star tier during this window means amplifying the noise at 2x. This rule caps all stocks at a lower tier during the discovery period, then promotes the top performer to Star once the dust settles.

forgeTemplates.text: During the first {minutes} minutes of EARLY phase, restrict maximum tier to {tier}. Promote top performer to Star after

minutes.label: Discovery period
minutes.hint: How long to restrict Star tier at the open. Longer = more data before committing the 2x multiplier.

tier.label: Morning max tier
tier.hint: Maximum tier during the discovery period. Core still provides some multiplier benefit.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will restrict the maximum tier during the first minutes of the EARLY phase, then promote the top-performing stock to Star once the restriction period ends.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Buy the dip to fair value
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Prefer stocks that have pulled back to VWAP in an uptrend — buying at institutional fair value.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: Smart money buys the dip to the average price
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: VWAP represents the average price institutions are paying throughout the day. When an uptrending stock pulls back to VWAP, it's offering a discount to institutional fair value. These pullbacks are high-probability entry points because big buyers tend to step in and defend the VWAP level.

forgeTemplates.text: Prefer stocks where price has pulled back to within {pct}% of daily VWAP while trend remains bullish

pct.label: VWAP pullback tolerance
pct.hint: How close to VWAP the price must pull back. Day traders use 0.2%, swing traders use 0.5%.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will prioritize stocks that have pulled back to within the specified percentage of their daily VWAP while maintaining a bullish overall trend.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Avoid overextended stocks
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Avoid stocks that have moved more than 2 standard deviations from VWAP.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: When a stock moves too far too fast from its average, it almost always comes back
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Stocks trading far above or below VWAP are statistically likely to revert to the mean. When price moves beyond 2 standard deviations from VWAP, the move is overextended and the risk of a reversal is high. This rule reduces selection priority for these stretched stocks to avoid buying at unsustainable prices.

forgeTemplates.text: Reduce selection priority for stocks trading beyond {dev} standard deviations from daily VWAP

dev.label: Overextension threshold
dev.hint: Standard deviations from VWAP before a stock is considered overextended. Higher = more room for winners to run.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will reduce selection priority for stocks trading beyond the specified number of standard deviations from their daily VWAP, avoiding overextended moves.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Follow institutional accumulation
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Prioritize stocks outperforming SPY — institutional accumulation signal.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: Stocks that hold up when the market drops are being accumulated by institutions
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Relative Strength vs. SPY measures how a stock performs compared to the broad market. Stocks with high relative strength are being accumulated by institutions — they hold up during selloffs and lead during rallies. This rule prioritizes market leaders and avoids laggards that can't keep up.

forgeTemplates.text: Prefer stocks with RS vs SPY score above {score}/22. Avoid stocks below {floor}

score.label: RS preference score
score.hint: Minimum Relative Strength vs SPY. Momentum riders use 18 (top 20%), swing traders use 17.

floor.label: RS avoidance floor
floor.hint: Below this score, the stock is avoided entirely. Higher = stricter quality filter.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will prefer stocks with Relative Strength vs. SPY scores above the specified threshold and avoid stocks scoring below the floor.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Catch the volatility squeeze
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Prioritize stocks with extremely narrow Bollinger Bands — about to explode.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: Quiet stocks are loading up energy — when the squeeze breaks, it's usually explosive
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: When Bollinger Bands contract to their narrowest width, it signals that volatility is being compressed like a spring. The subsequent breakout is often explosive and directional. Combined with above-average volume, a Bollinger squeeze is one of the most reliable breakout setups in technical analysis.

forgeTemplates.text: Prioritize stocks where Bollinger Band Width is in lowest {pct}th percentile, especially with volume above {vol}x average

pct.label: Squeeze tightness
pct.hint: How extreme the compression must be. 10th percentile = tighter than 90% of history.

vol.label: Volume confirmation multiplier
vol.hint: Volume above this multiple of average confirms the squeeze breakout.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will prioritize stocks with Bollinger Band Width in the lowest percentile of recent history, especially when accompanied by above-average volume signaling an imminent breakout.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Spot hidden momentum shifts
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Flags stocks where price and RSI disagree — momentum fading despite price looking strong.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: When momentum fades but price looks strong, a reversal is coming
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: RSI divergence occurs when price makes a new high but RSI makes a lower high (bearish) or price makes a new low but RSI makes a higher low (bullish). This disconnect between price and momentum is one of the earliest reversal warnings. This rule adjusts conviction based on divergence signals.

forgeTemplates.text: Reduce conviction in stocks showing bearish RSI divergence. Increase conviction for bullish divergence with {conviction} enforcement

conviction.label: Rule strength
conviction.hint: How strictly the agent follows this directive.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will detect RSI divergence patterns and adjust conviction accordingly — reducing it for bearish divergence and increasing it for bullish divergence.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Demand volume proof on breakouts
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Only trust breakouts with a volume spike — moves without volume are fake.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: A breakout without volume is a promise without action — demand proof
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: A price breakout is only meaningful if it's backed by significantly above-average volume. Volume confirms that institutions are participating in the move. Breakouts on normal or low volume are often false signals that quickly reverse. This rule filters out fake breakouts by requiring a volume spike.

forgeTemplates.text: Only act on breakouts where volume exceeds {mult}x the 20-day average

mult.label: Volume confirmation threshold
mult.hint: Volume must exceed this multiple of 20-day average for breakout to be valid. Higher = fewer but stronger signals.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will only act on breakout signals when volume exceeds the specified multiple of the 20-day average, filtering out false breakouts on thin volume.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Catch the narrowest range breakout
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Flag stocks with their narrowest daily range in 7 days — maximum energy compression.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: The quietest day in a week is usually followed by one of the loudest
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: NR7 (Narrow Range 7) flags stocks trading in their tightest daily range in seven sessions. Like a Bollinger squeeze, this compression signals stored energy that often releases in a powerful directional move. When combined with a strong technical score, NR7 stocks are prime breakout candidates.
