forgeTemplates.text: Prioritize stocks flagged with NR7 when combined with technical score above {score}

score.label: Technical score minimum
score.hint: NR7 stocks must also have a strong technical score. Higher = more selective breakout candidates.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will prioritize NR7-flagged stocks for portfolio selection when they also have a technical score above the specified threshold.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Require multiple green lights
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Require multiple indicators to agree before the agent acts — reduces false signals.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: One green light could be a fluke — three green lights mean the move is real
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Any single indicator can give a false signal. But when multiple independent indicators agree — price above VWAP, positive MACD histogram, and RSI in the bullish 50-70 range — the probability of a real move increases dramatically. This rule requires multi-signal confluence before your agent acts.

forgeTemplates.text: Only select stocks where at least {count} of these are bullish: price above VWAP, MACD histogram positive, RSI 50-70

count.label: Confluence requirement
count.hint: How many indicators must agree. 3 of 3 is the strongest filter but may miss some opportunities.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will only select stocks where the specified number of indicators are simultaneously bullish, filtering out false signals from single-indicator noise.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Ride the earnings surprise wave
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Prefer stocks that consistently beat earnings estimates by large margins.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: Companies that keep beating expectations keep surprising the market
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Post-Earnings Announcement Drift (PEAD) is one of the most well-documented market anomalies — stocks that beat earnings estimates tend to keep drifting in the surprise direction for weeks. This rule targets consistent big beaters, where the drift effect is strongest.

forgeTemplates.text: Prefer stocks where earnings beat rate exceeds {beat_pct}% and surprise magnitude is in top {decile}

beat_pct.label: Earnings beat rate
beat_pct.hint: Minimum percentage of quarters the company must have beaten estimates. Higher = more consistent beaters.

decile.label: Surprise magnitude
decile.hint: How large the earnings beats must be relative to peers. Top 10% finds the biggest upside surprises.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will prioritize stocks with high earnings beat rates and surprise magnitudes in the specified top percentile, capturing post-earnings announcement drift.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Trust the cash, not the math
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Prefer stocks with positive free cash flow — the real measure of financial health.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: Earnings can be faked with accounting tricks — cash flow can't
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Free cash flow is the cash a company generates after capital expenditures — it's much harder to manipulate than reported earnings. Companies with high FCF yield (FCF divided by market cap) are generating real money relative to their valuation, making them more resilient and less likely to disappoint.

forgeTemplates.text: Prefer stocks where FCF is positive and FCF yield is in top {pct}% of universe

pct.label: FCF yield percentile
pct.hint: Top percentile of FCF yield to target. Lower = more selective, finds the best cash generators.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will prioritize stocks with positive free cash flow and FCF yield in the top percentile of the universe, focusing on companies with genuine financial strength.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Avoid over-leveraged companies
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Avoid over-leveraged companies using sector-relative debt limits.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: A bank with 1.5x debt is normal — a tech company with 1.5x debt is a red flag
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Different sectors carry different amounts of debt as standard practice — financials are naturally leveraged while tech companies typically are not. This rule compares a company's debt-to-equity against its sector average rather than an absolute number, catching truly over-leveraged companies regardless of industry.

forgeTemplates.text: Avoid stocks where D/E exceeds {mult}x sector average. Tighten to {tight_mult}x when sentiment is bearish

mult.label: Normal leverage ceiling
mult.hint: Maximum D/E as multiple of sector average. Higher = more tolerant of leverage.

tight_mult.label: Bearish leverage ceiling
tight_mult.hint: Tighter ceiling during bearish sentiment. Lower = more defensive when markets are nervous.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will avoid stocks with debt-to-equity ratios exceeding the specified multiple of their sector average, tightening the threshold further during bearish sentiment.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Use the right valuation yardstick
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Uses the right valuation metric for each sector — P/B for banks, P/S for tech, dividend yield for utilities.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: You wouldn't judge a fish by how well it climbs a tree — use the right yardstick
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: P/E ratios are meaningless for unprofitable growth companies. P/B is the standard for banks. P/S works best for high-growth tech. Dividend yield matters most for utilities. This rule routes each stock to the valuation metric that actually matters for its sector, then selects the cheapest stocks on the correct measure.

forgeTemplates.text: Evaluate stocks using the metric appropriate to their sector. Prefer stocks in cheapest {pct}% on correct metric

pct.label: Value percentile
pct.hint: Prefer stocks in cheapest X% on their sector-appropriate metric. Lower = stricter value filter.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will evaluate each stock using the valuation metric most appropriate for its sector and prefer stocks ranking in the cheapest percentile on that metric.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Chase accelerating growth
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Prefer stocks where the growth rate is accelerating, not just high.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: Acceleration beats speed — growing 10% after 8% is better than 15% after 20%
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: A company growing revenue at 10% after growing at 8% last quarter is accelerating — the trend is improving. A company growing at 15% after 20% is decelerating — the trend is worsening. Markets reward acceleration because it signals improving business conditions and often leads to upward estimate revisions.

forgeTemplates.text: Prefer stocks where current revenue growth rate is at least {bps} basis points higher than previous quarter

bps.label: Acceleration threshold
bps.hint: Basis points of revenue growth acceleration required. Higher = only the strongest accelerators.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will prefer stocks showing revenue growth acceleration — where the current quarter's growth rate exceeds the previous quarter's by the specified number of basis points.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Follow the analyst upgrades
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Prefer stocks where analyst consensus has improved recently.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: When Wall Street upgrades in unison, they know something the market hasn't priced in
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Analyst estimate revisions are one of the strongest predictors of near-term stock performance. When multiple analysts simultaneously raise their estimates, they're responding to new information the market hasn't fully priced. This rule captures the revision momentum signal before the broader market catches up.

forgeTemplates.text: Prefer stocks where analyst consensus has improved over past {days} days. Avoid deteriorating consensus

days.label: Revision lookback
days.hint: How far back to check for analyst consensus changes. Shorter = more responsive to recent upgrades.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will prefer stocks with improving analyst consensus over the specified period and avoid stocks where consensus is deteriorating.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Manage earnings week risk
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Adjusts selection priority based on proximity to earnings dates.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: Earnings week is like a coin flip on steroids
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Earnings announcements create massive gap risk — stocks can jump or drop 10%+ overnight. This rule lets you control how your agent handles stocks approaching their earnings date. The default is to reduce priority (avoid the coin flip), but you can override for stocks with high historical beat rates.

forgeTemplates.text: Within {days} days of earnings, {action} selection priority. Override if beat rate above {beat_pct}%

days.label: Earnings proximity window
days.hint: Days before earnings to adjust priority. Larger window = earlier positioning.

action.label: Default earnings action
action.hint: How to handle stocks approaching earnings. Decrease avoids the gap risk, increase bets on the report.

beat_pct.label: Override beat rate
beat_pct.hint: Beat rate above which the default action is overridden. Only relevant if default is decrease.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will adjust selection priority for stocks approaching earnings dates based on the specified action, with an override for stocks exceeding the beat rate threshold.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Cap sector exposure
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Limits the number of stocks from any single sector.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: When one sector tanks, you don't want half your portfolio going with it
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Sector concentration is one of the most common portfolio killers. If three of your five stocks are tech and tech drops 5%, your whole portfolio suffers. This rule caps the maximum number of stocks from any single sector, forcing diversification that protects you from sector-specific shocks.

forgeTemplates.text: Limit portfolio to maximum of {max} stocks from any single sector

max.label: Maximum stocks per sector
max.hint: Hard cap on stocks from any single sector. Lower = more diversified but less ability to concentrate in hot sectors.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will enforce a maximum number of stocks from any single sector when building and rebalancing the portfolio.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Avoid hidden correlation traps
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Avoids holding multiple stocks from the same sub-industry.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: Three chip stocks isn't diversification — it's a triple bet on semiconductors
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Sector diversification isn't enough — two semiconductor stocks in different ETF sectors still move together. This rule goes deeper, treating stocks from the same sub-industry as highly correlated and limiting overlap. True diversification means different business drivers, not just different ticker symbols.

forgeTemplates.text: Avoid holding more than {max} stock from the same sub-industry

max.label: Sub-industry limit
max.hint: Maximum stocks from the same sub-industry. 1 ensures true diversification within sectors.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will limit holdings from the same sub-industry to the specified maximum, preventing hidden correlation from undermining portfolio diversification.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Mix stability with explosiveness
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Ensures mix of large-cap stability and small-cap volatility.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: Big stocks keep you alive, small stocks make you rich — you need both
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Large-cap stocks provide stability and predictable scoring, while small-caps deliver the explosive moves needed to hit high thresholds. A barbell strategy combines both extremes — large-cap anchors that protect your baseline score and small-cap satellites that provide upside potential.

forgeTemplates.text: Maintain at least {anchors} large-cap stocks and no more than {sails} small-cap stocks

anchors.label: Large-cap anchors
anchors.hint: Minimum number of stable large-cap stocks. More anchors = more baseline protection.

sails.label: Small-cap limit
sails.hint: Maximum number of volatile small-cap stocks. Fewer = less explosive risk.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will maintain a minimum number of large-cap anchor stocks and cap the number of small-cap stocks, ensuring a barbell mix of stability and explosive potential.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Switch to survival mode
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Shifts to defensive mode if total portfolio drops below a threshold.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: When the whole portfolio is bleeding, stop trying to be a hero
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: When your total portfolio drawdown exceeds a critical level, something has gone systemically wrong — the market regime may have shifted or your strategy is mismatched with conditions. This circuit breaker shifts to defensive mode, restricting new swaps to low-volatility stocks only until conditions stabilize.

forgeTemplates.text: If total portfolio drawdown exceeds {pct}%, shift to defensive mode with low-ATR stocks only

pct.label: Drawdown trigger
pct.hint: Portfolio loss percentage that triggers survival mode. Lower = earlier defensive shift.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will shift to defensive mode when total portfolio drawdown exceeds the specified percentage, restricting new swaps to low-ATR stocks only.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: De-risk in volatile markets
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Reduces high-ATR exposure when the broad market is in a volatile regime.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: When the whole market is panicking, even good stocks get dragged down
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: In high-volatility market regimes, correlations spike and even fundamentally strong stocks get dragged down. This rule detects elevated market volatility and restricts the portfolio to lower-ATR stocks, reducing exposure to the wild swings that can devastate a portfolio in chaotic conditions.

forgeTemplates.text: When market volatility is elevated, restrict portfolio to stocks with ATR below {pct}% of price

pct.label: ATR/price cap
pct.hint: Maximum ATR as percentage of price during volatile markets. Lower = only the calmest stocks allowed.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will restrict the portfolio to stocks with ATR below the specified percentage of price when broad market volatility is elevated.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Keep crypto on a leash
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Manages the mandatory crypto asset to prevent portfolio-destroying volatility.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: Crypto can make or break your battle — keep it on a leash
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Crypto assets are mandatory in the portfolio but carry extreme volatility. An uncontrolled crypto position in Star tier can single-handedly swing your score by 50+ points. This rule restricts crypto to a lower tier and limits exposure to major coins during portfolio drawdowns.

forgeTemplates.text: Restrict mandatory crypto to {tier} tier. During drawdowns, limit to major coins only

tier.label: Crypto tier cap
tier.hint: Maximum tier for the mandatory crypto asset. Support removes the multiplier entirely.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will restrict the mandatory crypto asset to the specified tier and limit to major coins only during portfolio drawdowns.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Avoid sectors in the news doghouse
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Excludes stocks in sectors with negative FantasyTimes sentiment.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: Don't fight the news — if FantasyTimes says a sector is in trouble, listen
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: FantasyTimes sentiment reflects the current news narrative around each sector. Fighting negative sentiment is a losing battle — even fundamentally strong stocks get dragged down when their sector is under fire. This rule excludes stocks from sectors with bearish or worse sentiment, keeping your portfolio aligned with the prevailing narrative.

forgeTemplates.text: Avoid buying stocks in sectors where FantasyTimes sentiment is {sentiment} or worse

sentiment.label: Sentiment exclusion floor
sentiment.hint: Minimum sentiment to allow buying. Neutral is stricter — only buys into bullish sectors.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will exclude stocks from sectors where FantasyTimes sentiment is at or below the specified level, avoiding sectors under negative news pressure.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Build a barbell portfolio
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Split portfolio between high-ATR explosive stocks and low-ATR anchors — avoid the moderate middle.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: Safe stocks keep you in the game, explosive stocks win it — need both extremes
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: A barbell portfolio combines two extremes: low-ATR anchor stocks that protect your baseline score and high-ATR rockets that chase explosive threshold bonuses. The boring middle ground — moderate stocks that neither protect nor explode — is the worst of both worlds in a single-day battle.

forgeTemplates.text: Build portfolio with at least {anchors} low-ATR anchors (below {low_pct}%) and {rockets} high-ATR rockets (above {high_pct}%)

anchors.label: Low-ATR anchors
anchors.hint: Minimum stable, low-volatility stocks for baseline protection.

rockets.label: High-ATR rockets
rockets.hint: Number of explosive, high-volatility stocks for threshold-chasing upside.

low_pct.label: Anchor ATR ceiling
low_pct.hint: Maximum ATR % of price for anchor stocks. Lower = calmer anchors.

high_pct.label: Rocket ATR floor
high_pct.hint: Minimum ATR % of price for rocket stocks. Higher = more explosive picks.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will build a barbell portfolio with the specified number of low-ATR anchor stocks and high-ATR explosive stocks, avoiding moderate-volatility stocks in between.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Lean into market leaders
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Overweight stocks with the highest relative strength — lean into the market leaders.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: Stocks beating the market today tend to keep beating it tomorrow — lean into leaders
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Momentum is the most persistent factor in equity markets — stocks with high relative strength tend to continue outperforming. This rule tilts your portfolio toward market leaders by requiring minimum RS scores for selection and reserving Star and Core tiers for the strongest performers.

forgeTemplates.text: Prefer stocks with RS vs SPY above {rs_min}/22. Star and Core only for top {pct}% RS

rs_min.label: Minimum RS score
rs_min.hint: Minimum Relative Strength vs SPY for selection. Higher = only the strongest market leaders.

pct.label: Top RS for premium tiers
pct.hint: Only stocks in the top X% of RS rankings get Star or Core. Lower = more exclusive.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will prefer stocks with RS vs. SPY above the minimum threshold and restrict Star and Core tier assignments to stocks in the top percentile of RS rankings.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Balance defense and offense
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Ensure a mix of high-ATR growth engines and high-fundamental-score defensive anchors.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: Growth stocks chase thresholds, defensive stocks protect the score — balance your appetite
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Growth stocks with high ATR chase the big threshold bonuses, while defensive stocks with strong fundamentals protect your baseline score from collapsing. The right balance depends on your risk appetite — more defensive stocks for safety, more growth stocks for upside.

forgeTemplates.text: Maintain at least {defensive} high-fundamental-score stocks and up to {growth} high-ATR growth stocks

defensive.label: Defensive stock count
defensive.hint: Minimum high-fundamental-score stocks for baseline protection.

growth.label: Growth stock limit
growth.hint: Maximum high-ATR growth stocks. More = higher upside but more risk.

fund_min.label: Fundamental score floor
fund_min.hint: Minimum composite fundamental score for defensive picks. Higher = stricter quality.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will maintain a minimum number of high-fundamental-score defensive stocks and cap the number of high-ATR growth stocks, balancing protection and upside.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Ride the sentiment tailwinds
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Overweight sectors with positive FantasyTimes sentiment — ride the narrative tailwinds.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: When the news cycle turns on a sector, the smart money moves first — move with it
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: FantasyTimes sentiment reflects the current news narrative for each sector. Sectors with bullish sentiment benefit from institutional buying pressure as the narrative drives capital flows. This rule overweights favored sectors and rebalances when sentiment shifts, keeping your portfolio aligned with the dominant market story.

forgeTemplates.text: Overweight sectors where FantasyTimes sentiment is {sentiment} or better

sentiment.label: Sentiment threshold
sentiment.hint: Minimum FantasyTimes sentiment for sector overweighting. Neutral is less selective but catches more sectors.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will overweight sectors with FantasyTimes sentiment at or above the specified level and rebalance when sentiment changes.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Build a versatile bench
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Build the bench to complement the active roster — different sectors, different styles.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: Your bench isn't a backup squad — it's a toolkit for when the market changes
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: A bench that mirrors your active roster is useless — when your picks are struggling, your bench will be too. This rule builds a complementary bench with different sector exposure and high-ATR breakout candidates, giving you real optionality when market conditions shift.

forgeTemplates.text: At least {complement} bench stocks from different sectors. Include {high_upside} high-ATR breakout candidates

complement.label: Cross-sector bench stocks
complement.hint: Minimum bench stocks from different sectors than the active roster. Higher = more diversified swap options.

high_upside.label: High-ATR bench candidates
high_upside.hint: Number of explosive breakout candidates to keep on the bench for momentum swaps.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will build a bench with stocks from different sectors than the active roster and include high-ATR breakout candidates for swap optionality.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Position for economic events
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Tilt the portfolio toward event-sensitive sectors ahead of major economic announcements.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: Big economic announcements move entire sectors — be positioned before the news drops
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Major economic events like FOMC decisions, CPI releases, and jobs reports create predictable sector-level moves. Rate-sensitive sectors react to Fed decisions, consumer sectors to CPI data, and so on. This rule tilts your portfolio toward the sectors historically most affected by upcoming events.

forgeTemplates.text: When high-impact event is within {days} days, tilt toward historically sensitive sectors

days.label: Event proximity window
days.hint: Days before a high-impact event to start positioning. Larger window = earlier preparation.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will tilt portfolio allocation toward sectors historically sensitive to upcoming high-impact economic events within the specified time window.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: RSI Momentum Zone
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Targets stocks in the RSI sweet spot — strong momentum without overextension. Unlike the oversold bounce, this rule seeks stocks already moving.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: The best stocks aren't oversold or overbought — they're in the power zone where momentum is building
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: RSI is often used to find oversold bounces, but quantitative research shows it works even better as a trend-following tool. Stocks with RSI between 50 and 70 are in a momentum sweet spot — strong enough to confirm a trend, but not so stretched that a pullback is imminent. This rule targets that power zone and avoids both weak (below 40) and overextended (above 75) stocks.

forgeTemplates.text: Prefer stocks with 14-day RSI between {low} and {high}. This zone indicates building momentum without overextension. Deprioritize stocks with RSI below {weak} (no momentum) or above {stretched} (overextended)

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will prioritize stocks with RSI in the 50-70 momentum zone and deprioritize stocks with weak or overextended RSI readings.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: MACD Histogram Acceleration
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Focuses on whether the MACD histogram is growing or shrinking. A growing histogram means momentum is accelerating — the move is getting stronger.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: A positive MACD is good, but a GROWING MACD is better — acceleration beats direction
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Most traders only check whether MACD is positive or negative. But the real edge is in the histogram's rate of change — is it growing or shrinking? A growing histogram means the gap between the MACD line and signal line is widening, which indicates accelerating momentum. When the histogram starts shrinking, even if still positive, the move is losing steam and a reversal may be near.

forgeTemplates.text: Prefer stocks where the MACD histogram is positive AND growing (current bar larger than previous). When the histogram starts shrinking, even if still positive, {action}

action.label: On deceleration
action.hint: What to do when momentum peaks

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will favor stocks with a growing MACD histogram and take the specified action when histogram momentum decelerates.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: MACD Zero-Line Bounce
forgeRuleTemplates.description: In an uptrend, MACD often pulls back toward zero then bounces. This catches the momentum reset before the next leg up.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: When momentum cools to neutral in an uptrend, the next surge is loading — buy the pause
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: In a healthy uptrend, momentum doesn't stay at maximum forever — it naturally oscillates. When the MACD histogram pulls back toward zero, many traders panic and sell. But if the daily trend structure (technical score) remains healthy, this pause is actually the momentum resetting before the next leg higher. This rule prevents your agent from mistaking a normal momentum pullback for a trend reversal.

forgeTemplates.text: When a stock's MACD histogram is near zero but the daily technical score is above {score}, treat this as a momentum pause in an uptrend — increase hold patience to {minutes} minutes. This is a buying opportunity, not an exit signal

score.label: Min daily score
score.hint: Confirms the trend is still healthy

minutes.label: Hold patience
minutes.hint: How long to wait for momentum to resume

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will hold through MACD zero-line pauses when the daily technical score confirms the uptrend is intact, increasing hold patience instead of swapping.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: VWAP Reclaim Entry
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Targets stocks that dipped below VWAP and recovered back above it. The reclaim signals buyers stepping in at institutional fair value.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: A stock that fights its way back above VWAP just proved the buyers are stronger than the sellers
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: VWAP (Volume-Weighted Average Price) represents the average price institutions paid throughout the day. When a stock dips below VWAP and then recovers above it, it signals that buyers stepped in at the institutional fair value level and overwhelmed sellers. This reclaim pattern is one of the most reliable intraday reversal signals because it demonstrates genuine buying pressure at a meaningful price level.

forgeTemplates.text: On the bench, prioritize stocks that have recently reclaimed VWAP from below (currently above VWAP with a VWAP deviation above {dev}% after previously being negative). This reversal pattern signals institutional buying

dev.label: Min deviation above VWAP
dev.hint: How far above VWAP to confirm reclaim

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will prioritize bench stocks showing a VWAP reclaim pattern — dipping below and recovering above VWAP with sufficient deviation to confirm the reversal.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Squeeze Direction Filter
forgeRuleTemplates.description: When a Bollinger Band squeeze is detected, use MACD histogram direction to predict breakout direction. Positive histogram = likely upward breakout.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: A squeeze tells you WHEN the move is coming — MACD tells you WHICH WAY
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: A Bollinger Band squeeze occurs when the bands contract tightly around price, indicating low volatility that typically precedes a big move. The problem is that squeezes break in both directions — up or down. By combining the squeeze detection with MACD histogram direction, you can filter for squeezes most likely to break upward. This is the core concept behind LazyBear's Squeeze Momentum Indicator, the most popular community script on TradingView.

forgeTemplates.text: When a stock is in a Bollinger squeeze (bandwidth below {bw}%), only select it if the MACD histogram is {direction}. A squeeze with negative momentum predicts a downward breakout — avoid

bw.label: Squeeze bandwidth
bw.hint: Lower = tighter squeeze = bigger expected move

direction.label: Required MACD state
direction.hint: How strong must the directional signal be

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will only select stocks in a Bollinger squeeze when the MACD histogram confirms a likely upward breakout direction, filtering out bearish squeezes.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Bollinger Lower Band Entry
forgeRuleTemplates.description: When price touches or penetrates the lower Bollinger Band, the stock is stretched below its statistical mean. Expect a bounce back toward the middle band.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: Stocks that touch the lower band are statistically stretched — the rubber band usually snaps back
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Bollinger Bands plot two standard deviations above and below a 20-period moving average. When price reaches the lower band, it's statistically at an extreme — roughly 95% of price action occurs within the bands. While a stock can "ride the band" in a strong downtrend, in normal conditions a touch of the lower band represents a high-probability mean reversion opportunity back toward the middle band (20 SMA).

forgeTemplates.text: Look for stocks where Bollinger percentB is below {percentB}. These are trading near or below the lower band and are mean-reversion candidates. Set exit expectation at the middle band (20 SMA). {tierRule}

percentB.label: Max percentB
percentB.hint: 0 = at the lower band, negative = below it

tierRule.label: Tier restriction
tierRule.hint: Mean reversion upside is defined, not explosive

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will target stocks trading near or below the lower Bollinger Band as mean-reversion candidates, with tier restrictions reflecting the defined upside.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Intraday Range Position
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Stocks that close near the low of their intraday range often bounce the next session. This is the IBS (Internal Bar Strength) concept from quantitative research.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: A stock beaten down to its daily low is spring-loaded for a morning bounce — this is one of the most backtested edges in quant trading
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Internal Bar Strength (IBS) measures where a stock's closing price falls within its intraday high-low range. Research across decades of data shows that stocks closing near their daily low tend to bounce the following session, while stocks closing near their high tend to pull back. This mean-reversion effect is one of the most robust edges in quantitative finance and works particularly well on liquid, large-cap stocks.

forgeTemplates.text: When a stock closes in the bottom {pct}% of its intraday range, increase hold patience to {minutes} minutes. A morning recovery is statistically likely. Do not swap a stock near its daily low unless it breaches a Bust threshold

pct.label: Bottom range %
pct.hint: Lower = more extreme = higher bounce probability

minutes.label: Bounce patience
minutes.hint: How long to wait for the recovery

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will increase hold patience for stocks closing near the bottom of their intraday range, giving the statistically likely morning bounce time to develop.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Low Volume Pullback Hold
forgeRuleTemplates.description: In an uptrend, pullbacks on below-average volume are healthy — they show a lack of selling pressure. The trend resumes when volume returns.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: If nobody's actually selling, the dip isn't real — low volume pullbacks in uptrends are gifts
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Volume tells you the conviction behind a price move. When a stock in an uptrend pulls back on below-average volume, it means there's no real selling pressure — the pullback is caused by a temporary absence of buyers, not an influx of sellers. These low-volume dips typically resolve when normal buying volume returns. Conversely, if volume INCREASES during a pullback, institutional sellers are participating and the dip may be real.

forgeTemplates.text: When a stock in an uptrend (daily technical score above {score}) pulls back on below-average volume (volume ratio below {vol}x), increase hold patience to {minutes} minutes. Only swap if volume INCREASES during the pullback

score.label: Min trend score
score.hint: Confirms the stock is still in an uptrend

vol.label: Max volume ratio
vol.hint: Below this = low volume = healthy pullback

minutes.label: Extra patience
minutes.hint: How long to hold during the low-volume dip

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will hold through pullbacks on low volume in uptrending stocks, only considering a swap if volume increases during the decline.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Smart Money Liquidity Sweep
forgeRuleTemplates.description: When a stock drops sharply on a volume spike then immediately recovers, institutional players swept stop-losses to accumulate at a lower price. Hold through this pattern.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: That scary drop and instant recovery? That was smart money shaking out weak hands to buy cheaper
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Liquidity sweeps are a core concept in Smart Money / ICT (Inner Circle Trader) methodology. Large institutions need to accumulate shares without driving the price up, so they deliberately push price through a support level to trigger stop-loss orders. This creates a burst of selling liquidity that they absorb. The telltale sign: a sharp drop on elevated volume followed by a quick recovery back above VWAP. If your stock shows this pattern, the "dip" was engineered — hold through it.

forgeTemplates.text: When a stock drops more than {atr}x ATR intraday on elevated volume (above {vol}x average) but then recovers above VWAP within {minutes} minutes, do NOT swap — this is a liquidity sweep pattern. Increase hold conviction

atr.label: Drop threshold
atr.hint: How far the stock must drop to trigger this pattern

vol.label: Volume spike
vol.hint: Volume must be elevated for a true sweep

minutes.label: Recovery window
minutes.hint: How quickly it must recover to confirm the pattern

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will recognize liquidity sweep patterns — sharp drops on volume followed by VWAP recovery — and hold through them instead of panic-swapping.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Earnings + Technical Confluence
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Stocks with both strong earnings history AND bullish technicals have dual confirmation. Fundamental quality backs the technical momentum.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: Great earnings AND great technicals? That's the market saying "this stock deserves to be here" — double conviction
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: The strongest stock picks have both fundamental quality and technical momentum. A stock with great earnings but weak technicals may be a value trap — the market knows something the numbers don't show. A stock with strong technicals but weak fundamentals may be a speculative bubble. When both signals agree, you have dual confirmation that the stock's price action is backed by real business performance.

forgeTemplates.text: Prefer stocks where the fundamental composite score is above {fund_score} AND the daily technical score is above {tech_score}. Stocks meeting both criteria are eligible for {tier} tier. Stocks meeting only one are restricted to Core or below

tier.label: Dual-confirm tier
tier.hint: What tier can dual-confirmed stocks reach

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will require both strong fundamentals and strong technicals for Star tier eligibility, restricting single-signal stocks to Core or below.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: 52-Week High Breakout Preference
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Stocks near their 52-week high are breaking through resistance. This is the Donchian / channel breakout concept — new highs attract momentum buyers.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: Stocks making new highs tend to keep making new highs — resistance becomes support once it breaks
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: The Donchian Channel breakout strategy is one of the oldest and most respected trend-following systems. When a stock approaches or breaks its 52-week high, it's clearing a major resistance level that attracts momentum-following institutional capital. Contrary to the instinct that "it's too high to buy," stocks near their highs tend to continue higher because the breakout signals that all overhead supply has been absorbed.

forgeTemplates.text: Prefer stocks with a highProximity score above {score} out of 12. Stocks within {pct}% of their 52-week high are in breakout territory and attract momentum-following institutional buyers

pct.label: Max distance from high
pct.hint: How close to the 52-week high to qualify

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will prefer stocks trading near their 52-week high, using highProximity scores to identify breakout candidates with institutional momentum.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Multi-Factor Tier Assignment
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Assigns tiers based on how many independent signals agree. More confirmations = higher tier. Stocks that only pass one check get the lowest tier.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: One green light is a suggestion. Three green lights is conviction — let the evidence decide your tier
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Alexander Elder's Triple Screen system and the MACD+RSI+Volume "Trinity" are among the most recommended indicator combinations on TradingView. The insight: no single indicator is reliable alone, but when three independent signals agree, the probability of a winning trade increases dramatically. This rule checks three factors — daily technical score, RSI momentum zone, and volume — and assigns tiers based on how many pass.

forgeTemplates.text: Check each stock against three factors: (1) Daily technical score above {tech}, (2) RSI in momentum zone {rsi_low}-{rsi_high}, (3) Volume above {vol}x average. Assign Star to stocks passing all 3. Core to stocks passing 2. Support to stocks passing 1 or 0

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will assign tiers based on how many of three independent factors each stock passes — daily technical score, RSI momentum zone, and volume confirmation.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Volume Spike Institutional Signal
forgeRuleTemplates.description: When volume explodes above 2x average on a bullish candle, institutions are taking a position. This is the strongest confirmation signal in technical analysis.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: When the big money shows up, the volume screams it — a 2x spike on a green candle is the loudest buy signal in the market
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Volume spikes are the fingerprint of institutional activity. When volume surges to 2x or more of the 20-day average on a positive price move, it indicates that large players — mutual funds, hedge funds, pension funds — are actively accumulating. This is the strongest form of technical confirmation because it represents real capital commitment, not just pattern interpretation. Retail traders can't move volume like this.

forgeTemplates.text: When evaluating bench stocks for swaps, prioritize any stock showing a volume spike above {mult}x the 20-day average with positive price action. This overrides other technical signals — volume is the ultimate confirmation. Assign these stocks a minimum tier of {tier}

mult.label: Spike multiplier
mult.hint: How much above average to qualify as a spike

tier.label: Min tier on spike
tier.hint: Volume conviction should be rewarded with tier placement

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will prioritize bench stocks with volume spikes above the specified multiplier on bullish price action, assigning a minimum tier floor to reflect institutional conviction.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Sector Leader Selection
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Instead of picking stocks first, identify the strongest sectors then pick the leader within each one. Ride the sector tide and the stock wave simultaneously.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: A great stock in a bad sector is swimming against the current — find the strongest sector first, then pick its champion
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Sector rotation is a major driver of stock returns — studies show that sector selection explains more of a stock's performance than individual stock selection alone. By first identifying the strongest sectors using sector RS scores, then selecting the leader within each sector using RS vs SPY, you align both the macro and micro forces in your favor. This is the institutional approach: top-down sector allocation with bottom-up stock picking.

forgeTemplates.text: Overweight sectors with the highest sector RS scores. Within each strong sector, select the stock with the highest RS vs SPY score. Limit exposure to any single sector to {max_pct}%. When FantasyTimes reports sector rotation, adjust within {evals} evaluations

evals.label: Rotation speed
evals.hint: How quickly to respond to sector shifts

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will overweight the strongest sectors by RS score, select the leading stock within each, and respond to FantasyTimes sector rotation signals within the specified evaluation window.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Threshold Harvest Swap
forgeRuleTemplates.description: After a stock hits a BaggerBomb threshold bonus, immediately evaluate whether to swap it for a fresh high-ATR candidate. The points are banked — now find the next threshold opportunity.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: You already got the +15. The stock doesn't know it owes you another one — swap for a fresh rocket
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: BaggerBomb scoring thresholds award bonus points when a stock moves a certain multiple of its ATR. Once those points are banked, the stock has no memory of owing you more — it's equally likely to move toward the next threshold or to reverse. Meanwhile, a fresh high-ATR bench stock with bullish momentum has its full threshold journey ahead of it. This harvest swap strategy optimizes for multiple threshold hits across different stocks rather than waiting for one epic move.

forgeTemplates.text: After a stock triggers a {threshold} threshold bonus, swap it out within {evals} evaluations for the highest-ATR bench stock with bullish momentum (RSI above {rsi} and above VWAP). The scored points are locked — maximize remaining time by finding the next threshold candidate

evals.label: Swap speed
evals.hint: Evaluations before executing the harvest swap

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Your agent will swap out stocks that have triggered a scoring threshold bonus, replacing them with the highest-ATR bench candidate showing bullish momentum to chase the next threshold hit.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Institutional Conviction Filter
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Prefer stocks where active institutional holders are net accumulating. Filters out passive index fund noise to focus on informed, high-conviction buying.
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Institutional conviction is measured by weighting each holder's quarterly change by their portfolio concentration. A stock showing "strong accumulation" means multiple active fund managers are increasing positions as a significant percentage of their portfolios — not just index funds mechanically rebalancing. Research shows that a manager's most over-weighted positions outperform the market by 1.6-2.1% per quarter.

forgeTemplates.text: Strongly prefer drafting stocks where institutional conviction is {conviction}

conviction.label: Minimum Conviction Level
conviction.hint: Strong filters out passive index inflows. Mild is more permissive but noisier.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Filters the draft universe to stocks where active institutional holders (excluding passive index funds) are net accumulating. Uses the weighted conviction score from 13F filings. This is a soft preference — the agent can still draft stocks without institutional backing if technical signals are strong.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Distribution Avoidance
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Strictly avoid stocks where institutions are actively selling. When smart money exits, overhead supply caps intraday upside and increases bust risk.
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Institutional distribution creates a "VWAP ceiling" — when large funds are selling, their algorithms feed sell orders into any price rally, suppressing the momentum needed for ATR threshold crossings. Research shows that sell herding has a more persistent negative impact on returns than buy herding has a positive impact. This asymmetry makes distribution avoidance one of the most effective defensive rules.

forgeTemplates.text: Strictly avoid drafting stocks where institutional conviction is {level} or worse

level.label: Avoidance Threshold
level.hint: Strong Distribution filters the bottom ~10-15%. Mild Distribution is more aggressive and removes ~25-30%.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Hard filter that excludes stocks from the draftable universe when institutional holders are net selling. This is a defensive rule — stocks under active distribution face overhead selling pressure from institutional VWAP algorithms that cap intraday upside. Applied at draft time as a Level 1 filter.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Consensus Discovery
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Prefer stocks where multiple institutions opened brand new positions this quarter. New money entering a stock signals a fresh catalyst that passed rigorous research filters.
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: When an institution opens a new position, it means the stock competed for capital against every other opportunity in the manager's universe. When two or more do it independently in the same quarter, it signals a "consensus discovery" — multiple professional research teams found the same opportunity. This cluster buying pattern is one of the strongest alpha signals in 13F data.

forgeTemplates.text: Prefer stocks where at least {count} top-20 institutional holders initiated a completely new position this quarter

count.label: Minimum New Positions
count.hint: 1 is noise. 2 is consensus. 3+ is a stampede. Higher = stronger signal but fewer qualifying stocks.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Identifies stocks with fresh institutional interest — positions that didn't exist last quarter. Multiple new positions in the same stock signal a consensus discovery among independent research teams. Applied as a preference during portfolio construction.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Whale Concentration Guard
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Avoid stocks where a single institution holds too large a stake. When one whale controls the float, their exit creates outsized price drops and bust risk.
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: When a single entity controls 20%+ of outstanding shares, the stock's liquidity becomes dependent on that fund's stability. If the whale faces redemptions, their forced selling overwhelms market depth and triggers cascading price drops. The threshold of 20% accounts for the dominance of passive index providers (Vanguard, BlackRock, State Street), who routinely hold 10-15% of major stocks through mechanical index inclusion.

forgeTemplates.text: Avoid stocks where any single institutional entity holds more than {pct}% of total outstanding shares

pct.label: Maximum Single-Holder Stake
pct.hint: 20% filters extreme concentration while allowing normal passive index holdings. Lower = stricter but may exclude popular large-caps.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Tail-risk filter that excludes stocks with extreme ownership concentration by a single entity. Applied at draft time to prevent the agent from holding stocks vulnerable to a single fund's liquidation cascade. The 20% default accounts for passive index fund dominance in modern markets.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Active Fund Overlap Guard
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Prevent drafting too many stocks held by the same active mutual fund. High overlap means correlated drawdowns when that fund faces redemptions.
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: When multiple stocks in your portfolio are top holdings of the same active mutual fund, they become linked through common flow shocks. During market stress, funds facing redemptions liquidate across their entire portfolio simultaneously — creating correlated crashes in seemingly unrelated stocks. This rule targets active fund overlap specifically because passive index funds (Vanguard, BlackRock) hold everything and carry no informational signal.

forgeTemplates.text: Ensure no more than {max} drafted stocks share the same top-3 active mutual fund holder (excluding passive index providers)

max.label: Maximum Overlap
max.hint: 2 enforces strict diversification in a 5-stock portfolio. 3 allows moderate clustering. 1 is extremely restrictive.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Portfolio diversification rule that limits how many drafted stocks can share the same active mutual fund as a top-3 holder. Passive index funds are excluded from the check since they hold everything mechanically. Applied during portfolio construction to prevent correlated liquidation risk.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Hedge Fund Favorites
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Target stocks widely held by top hedge funds for momentum amplification. Crowded trades provide explosive intraday moves but carry reversal risk.
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Stocks held by multiple top hedge funds benefit from persistent buying pressure during momentum phases — the Goldman Sachs "Hedge Fund VIP" index outperforms the S&P 500 in 60% of quarters. However, these crowded positions are fragile: when market stress hits, highly correlated hedge funds unwind simultaneously, causing violent crashes. Use this rule for BaggerBomb momentum plays but pair it with tight technical swap parameters.

forgeTemplates.text: Target high-momentum setups in stocks held by at least {count} of the top-20 hedge funds, but maintain strict technical swap parameters due to crowded-trade reversal risk

count.label: Minimum Hedge Fund Holders
count.hint: 3 identifies a crowded trade. 5+ is an extremely popular position with high momentum but severe crash risk.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Momentum amplifier that prefers stocks widely held across top hedge funds. These "crowded trades" produce outsized intraday moves ideal for ATR threshold crossings. The agent must pair this with strict technical swap rules — if VWAP or 5-min MACD breaks down, exit immediately to avoid herd liquidation.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Sector Institutional Flow
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Align stock selection with sectors where institutional money is flowing in. Capital rotation at the sector level creates structural tailwinds for individual stocks.
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Institutions don't just pick stocks — they rotate capital along sector lines. When massive funds rotate into Technology or out of Financials, it creates a rising or falling tide that individual stocks can't fight. Sector-level flow has 71% directional accuracy in high-signal sectors like Energy. This rule stacks well with FantasyTimes news sentiment for double confirmation.

forgeTemplates.text: Prefer drafting stocks in sectors where the aggregate institutional flow sentiment is {sentiment}

sentiment.label: Sector Flow Threshold
sentiment.hint: Bullish aligns with the dominant capital rotation. Neutral allows sectors that aren't actively distributing.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Macro-alignment rule that ensures the agent's stock picks are in sectors where institutional capital is flowing in. Acts as a structural tailwind multiplier for technical breakout signals. Stacks with FantasyTimes sector sentiment for dual confirmation. Applied as a Level 2 preference during portfolio construction.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Insider + Institution Confluence
forgeRuleTemplates.description: The premium signal: prefer stocks where both institutional holders AND company insiders are buying. Dual confirmation from people with the deepest knowledge.
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: When corporate insiders (CEOs, CFOs) buy their own stock AND institutional managers are accumulating, it creates the strongest predictive signal in the 13F universe. Insiders know the company's immediate prospects; institutions validate the thesis with external analysis. Research shows this confluence yields 12-18% annualized abnormal returns. The 60-day insider lookback captures post-earnings buying windows while keeping the signal timely.

forgeTemplates.text: Highlight as highest-conviction: Strongly prefer stocks where institutional conviction is accumulating AND insider activity in the past {days} days shows net buying

days.label: Insider Lookback Window
days.hint: 60 days captures recent post-earnings insider buying. 90 is standard for longer horizons. 30 is aggressive and may miss slower-moving signals.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: The highest-ranked institutional rule. Combines lagged 13F institutional accumulation with near real-time insider buying (Form 4 filings, required within 2 business days). This confluence neutralizes the primary weakness of quarterly data by demanding a timely insider confirmation. Applied as the top priority during portfolio construction — stocks meeting this criteria get maximum draft preference.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Transient Capital Catalyst
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Prefer stocks where accumulation is driven by high-turnover, short-horizon institutions. These "transient" funds amplify intraday volatility — exactly what BaggerBomb rewards.
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Not all institutional money is equal. "Transient" institutions (high portfolio turnover, short holding periods) create significantly more stock return volatility than "dedicated" long-term holders. Since BaggerBomb rewards ATR threshold crossings, stocks with transient institutional accumulation are structurally more likely to produce the sharp intraday moves needed for Bagger bonuses. Dedicated holders provide stability but suppress the volatility BaggerBomb rewards.

forgeTemplates.text: Prefer stocks where recent institutional accumulation is driven by high-turnover transient institutions rather than long-term dedicated holders

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Volatility amplifier that biases the agent toward stocks with accumulation by high-turnover "transient" institutions (quantitative funds, short-horizon momentum funds) rather than low-turnover "dedicated" holders. Transient capital creates the sharp intraday price movements needed for ATR threshold crossings. This is a toggle rule with no parameters — the agent checks whether the accumulating institutions are classified as high-turnover in the archetype system.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Institutional Breadth Momentum
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Prefer stocks where the number of unique institutional holders is expanding quarter after quarter. A growing investor base often precedes major price re-ratings.
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Breadth of ownership — how many unique funds hold a stock — is often more informative than depth (how much they hold). A stock being adopted by 10-20 new funds each quarter for multiple consecutive quarters experiences a "geometric expansion" in its investor base. This expanding breadth typically precedes significant price re-ratings as the stock graduates from niche to mainstream institutional coverage.

forgeTemplates.text: Prefer stocks where the number of unique institutional holders has increased for at least {quarters} consecutive quarters

quarters.label: Consecutive Growth Quarters
quarters.hint: 2 confirms a trend. 3+ is a strong geometric expansion. 1 may be noise.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Identifies stocks with expanding institutional adoption — a growing number of unique fund holders over consecutive quarters. This "breadth momentum" often precedes significant price re-ratings as the stock moves from niche to mainstream institutional coverage. Applied as a preference during portfolio construction, particularly useful for mid-cap Rockets that are gaining institutional traction.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: RSI Entry Gate
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Only enter positions where RSI indicates the stock isn't overbought — prevents chasing stocks that have already run.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: Stops you from buying at the top — if everyone's already in, you're late
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: RSI measures momentum on a 0-100 scale. Stocks with high RSI have already rallied hard and are statistically more likely to pull back. By gating entries below a threshold, you avoid buying at the top of a move. In a 4-week season, getting caught in a pullback wastes precious runway. This pairs naturally with the Momentum Entry Threshold — together they define a "sweet spot" where stocks are moving but not overextended.

forgeTemplates.text: Only enter positions where RSI is below {upper}

upper.label: Max RSI
upper.hint: Lower = stricter. Below 60 is conservative, 70+ is permissive.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Blocks entry into stocks with RSI above the threshold. Prevents buying overbought momentum that may reverse.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Volume Confirmation
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Require meaningful trading volume before entering — ensures the stock has active interest, not a dead drift.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: Volume is conviction — if nobody's trading it, why are you buying it?
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Volume confirms that a price move has institutional participation behind it. Stocks drifting on low volume are prone to sudden reversals when real buyers or sellers arrive. By requiring above-average volume, you filter for stocks where institutions are actively engaged — the moves are more likely to sustain. In a season portfolio, getting stuck in a low-volume name that drifts sideways wastes a roster slot.

forgeTemplates.text: Require volume to be at least {multiplier}x the 20-day average before entering

multiplier.label: Volume Multiple
multiplier.hint: 1.0 = average volume. Higher = only buy on strong volume days.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Requires relative volume above threshold before entering a position. Filters out low-interest stocks.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Trend Alignment Filter
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Only buy stocks trading above their moving average — the simplest trend-following filter. Below the SMA = downtrend.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: Don't fight the trend — if it's below the average, the market is telling you something
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: A stock trading above its moving average is in an uptrend — momentum is on your side. A stock below it is fighting gravity. This is the most fundamental trend-following filter and forms the backbone of most systematic strategies. Shorter moving averages (20-day) react faster but produce more false signals. The 50-day is the institutional standard. The 200-day defines the major trend and rarely gives false readings.

forgeTemplates.text: Only enter stocks trading above their {period}-day moving average

period.label: Moving Average Period
period.hint: Shorter periods react faster but give more false signals.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Filters out stocks in downtrends by requiring price above the selected moving average period.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Earnings Avoidance Window
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Don't enter positions right before earnings — overnight gap risk can destroy a position. Huge strategic lever.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: Earnings are coin flips — great companies miss, bad companies surprise. Avoid the casino.
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Earnings announcements create massive gap risk — stocks can jump or drop 10%+ overnight regardless of quality. In a 4-week season, a single earnings gap against you can wipe out days of careful gains. This rule creates a buffer zone around earnings dates, preventing new entries when the risk/reward is dominated by a binary event. Conservative players use 5-10 day buffers; aggressive players accept 1-2 day windows.

forgeTemplates.text: Don't enter within {days} trading days of an earnings report

days.label: Buffer Days
days.hint: Conservative: 5-10 days. Aggressive: 1-2 days. This is a major risk control.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Blocks entry into stocks with earnings reports within the buffer window. Avoids overnight gap risk.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Fundamental Floor
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Require a minimum fundamental quality score — prevents chasing technically attractive junk.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: Charts lie, fundamentals don't — make sure the company is actually solid
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Technical signals can make a fundamentally weak stock look attractive — momentum, breakouts, and volume spikes happen in bad companies too. This rule sets a quality floor using the composite fundamental score (0-100), which combines earnings quality, revenue growth, balance sheet strength, and valuation metrics. Stocks below the floor are excluded regardless of how good the chart looks. A score of 50 is median quality; 70+ indicates strong fundamentals.

forgeTemplates.text: Only enter stocks with a Fundamental Score above {minScore}

minScore.label: Minimum Score
minScore.hint: Our scoring system rates fundamentals 0-100. 50 is median quality.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Requires minimum fundamental score before entry. Prevents buying technically attractive but fundamentally weak stocks.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Momentum Entry Threshold
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Require recent price momentum before entering — no dead money. Creates natural tension with the RSI gate.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: Money in motion stays in motion — flat stocks waste your limited season runway
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: In a 4-week season, every day counts. A stock that isn't moving is consuming a roster slot without contributing returns. This rule requires minimum recent price momentum before entry, ensuring your agent only buys stocks that are actively trending. The natural tension with the RSI Entry Gate is intentional — momentum requires the stock to be moving, but RSI caps how far it can have moved. Together they define the optimal entry window: moving but not overextended.

forgeTemplates.text: Require a minimum {period}-day price change of {pct}%

period.label: Lookback Period
period.hint: Shorter = recent momentum. Longer = sustained trend.

pct.label: Min Change %
pct.hint: Higher = stronger momentum required. Watch for tension with RSI Gate.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Requires minimum price change over the lookback period. Filters out stagnant stocks wasting season runway.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Sector Freshness Check
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Prevents sector concentration at entry time — if you already have 30% tech, don't add more tech.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: Diversification happens at the door, not after the house is on fire
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Sector concentration is one of the biggest portfolio killers in a multi-week season. If three of your positions are tech and tech drops 5%, your whole portfolio suffers. This rule checks sector exposure at entry time and blocks new positions when a sector is already at its weight cap. Unlike rebalancing rules that fix drift after it happens, this prevents concentration from forming in the first place.

forgeTemplates.text: Don't enter if sector already at {maxPct}% or more of portfolio

maxPct.label: Max Sector Weight
maxPct.hint: Lower = more diversified. 25-30% is moderate. 15% is very strict.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Blocks entry when a sector already exceeds the weight cap. Enforces diversification at entry time.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Institutional Sentiment Check
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Only enter stocks where big institutions are buying, not selling. Leverages 13F data as a leading indicator.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: Follow the smart money — if BlackRock is buying, they probably know something
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Institutional 13F filings reveal what the biggest money managers are doing with their portfolios. When institutions are increasing their positions, it signals confidence backed by deep research. When they're reducing, it often precedes price weakness. This rule checks the direction of institutional ownership over recent quarters — increasing or stable ownership is a green light, while declining ownership is a warning sign. The multi-quarter lookback filters out noise from single-quarter rebalancing.

forgeTemplates.text: Only enter stocks where institutional ownership has {direction} over the last {quarters} quarters

direction.label: Ownership Direction
direction.hint: Increased = bullish institutions. Stable = not bailing. Any = disabled.

quarters.label: Lookback Quarters
quarters.hint: More quarters = stronger conviction signal but slower to react.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Requires institutional ownership trending in the specified direction. Uses 13F data as a conviction signal.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Fixed Stop-Loss
forgeRuleTemplates.description: The most fundamental risk rule. Sell any position that drops a set percentage from entry. Tight stops = quick cuts + frequent re-entry. Wide stops = ride through volatility.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: The #1 rule in trading: cut your losses. The only question is where.
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Stop-losses are the single most important risk management tool. Without one, a small loss can snowball into a catastrophic one. The tradeoff is between tight and wide: tight stops (3-5%) cut losses quickly but trigger frequently, leading to more re-entry costs and whipsaws. Wide stops (15-20%) give positions room to breathe through normal volatility but expose you to larger drawdowns when the thesis is truly broken. In a 4-week season, a balanced stop around 7-10% gives enough room for daily noise while capping downside.

forgeTemplates.text: Sell any position that drops {pct}% from entry

pct.label: Stop-Loss %
pct.hint: Tight (3-5%) = frequent stops. Medium (7-10%) = balanced. Wide (15-20%) = ride volatility.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Mandatory sell when position drops below stop-loss threshold from entry price. Hard priority — overrides soft holds.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Trailing Stop
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Sell if position drops from its highest price since entry — protects gains by measuring from the peak, not the entry.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: Lock in gains automatically — you'll never give back your entire rally
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: A trailing stop ratchets upward with the stock price but never moves down. If a stock rises 20% then pulls back 10% from its peak, the trailing stop triggers — you keep 10% instead of watching all gains evaporate. The key tension is with Profit Target: a profit target sells at a fixed gain (e.g., +15%), while a trailing stop lets winners run indefinitely but gives back some gains on exit. Combining both creates a system where positions either hit the target or get stopped out on a reversal.

forgeTemplates.text: Sell if position drops {pct}% from its highest closing price since entry

pct.label: Trail Distance %
pct.hint: Tighter = protects more gain but exits sooner. Wider = lets winners breathe.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Sells when position drops from its high-water mark by the trail percentage. Hard priority. Protects accumulated gains.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Time-Based Exit
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Close positions that aren't working within a time window. Dead money in a 4-week season wastes 25% of your runway per week.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: Time is money — literally. A flat stock in a 20-day season is an expensive do-nothing.
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: In a 4-week season, time is your scarcest resource. A stock that sits flat for a week has consumed 25% of your season runway without contributing returns. This rule sets a performance deadline — if a position hasn't gained the minimum within the time window, it gets closed and the capital is redeployed to a better opportunity. The minimum gain threshold is the key lever: 0% means "just don't lose money," while 2%+ demands active profit generation.

forgeTemplates.text: Close any position that hasn't gained {pct}% within {days} trading days

days.label: Time Window
days.hint: Shorter = impatient but responsive. Longer = more patient.

pct.label: Min Gain Required
pct.hint: 0% = must not lose money. 2%+ = must actively profit.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Exits positions that fail to achieve minimum gain within the time window. Soft priority. Fights dead money.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Profit Target
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Sell when a position hits a gain target — birds in the hand. Natural tension with Trailing Stop (lock in now vs. let it run).
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: Nobody went broke taking profits — but leaving money on the table hurts too
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Profit targets create a disciplined exit at a predetermined gain level. The advantage is certainty — you lock in gains without waiting for a reversal signal. The disadvantage is capping upside — a stock that would have gained 40% gets sold at 15%. The key tension is with the Trailing Stop: if both are equipped, the tighter one fires first. A 15% profit target with a 10% trailing stop means the target fires first for a steady rise, but the trailing stop catches a sharp reversal before the target is reached.

forgeTemplates.text: Sell any position that gains {pct}% from entry

pct.label: Profit Target %
pct.hint: Low (5-8%) = frequent wins. High (20%+) = fewer but bigger wins.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Sells positions that reach the profit target. Soft priority. Locks in gains at a fixed level.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Technical Exit Signal
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Sell on technical breakdown — RSI overbought, MACD crossover, or price dropping below its moving average.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: Let the charts tell you when the party's over, not your gut
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Technical exit signals let the market tell you when a trend is ending rather than guessing. RSI overbought signals momentum exhaustion — the stock has risen too far too fast. MACD bearish crossover detects a shift in trend direction before it becomes obvious on the chart. Price below the moving average confirms the trend has broken. The "RSI OR MACD" option casts the widest net — either signal triggers an exit, making it the most defensive choice.

forgeTemplates.text: Sell on technical breakdown: {trigger}

trigger.label: Exit Trigger
trigger.hint: RSI = momentum reversal. MACD = trend shift. SMA = trend break.

rsiThreshold.label: RSI Threshold
rsiThreshold.hint: Only used with RSI trigger. Higher = more permissive.

smaPeriod.label: SMA Period
smaPeriod.hint: Only used with SMA trigger. 20-day reacts faster.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Exits on selected technical breakdown signal. Soft priority. Pairs with entry criteria for complete technical systems.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Earnings Exit
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Sell positions before earnings to avoid overnight gap risk. The toggle is the key decision: protect all positions or only profitable ones?
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: Take profits before the dice roll — or hold through and hope for the best
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Earnings reports create binary outcomes — stocks can gap 10%+ in either direction overnight. If you're sitting on a profitable position, selling before earnings locks in those gains and eliminates the risk of giving them back on a miss. The "Only If Profitable" toggle is the critical decision: ON means you protect gains but hold losers through earnings (hoping for a positive surprise), while OFF means you exit everything approaching earnings regardless of P&L — the more defensive choice.

forgeTemplates.text: Sell positions {days} days before earnings if profitable

days.label: Days Before Earnings
days.hint: More days = safer but may miss pre-earnings run-up.

onlyIfProfitable.label: Only If Profitable
onlyIfProfitable.hint: ON = protect gains only. OFF = also cut losers before potential further damage.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Exits positions approaching earnings reports. Toggle controls whether only profitable positions are sold or all positions.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Correlation-Based Exit
forgeRuleTemplates.description: If two holdings move together too closely, sell the weaker one. Sector diversity ≠ correlation diversity.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: Owning 3 tech stocks that move in lockstep isn't diversification — it's triple exposure
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Two stocks can be in different sectors yet still move in lockstep — for example, a cloud software company and a semiconductor maker might both track the Nasdaq closely. High rolling correlation between holdings means your diversification is illusory — when one drops, the other drops too. This rule computes pairwise correlation over the specified window and sells the weaker performer when two holdings exceed the threshold. True portfolio diversification requires low correlation, not just different ticker symbols.

forgeTemplates.text: If two holdings show {days}-day correlation above {threshold}, sell the weaker one

days.label: Correlation Window
days.hint: Shorter = catches recent convergence. Longer = structural similarity.

threshold.label: Correlation Threshold
threshold.hint: 0.85 is high correlation. Lower = stricter diversification.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Compares rolling correlation between all position pairs. Sells the weaker of any pair exceeding the threshold. Soft priority.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Position Size Cap
forgeRuleTemplates.description: Trim any position that grows too large — classic rebalancing. The gap between max and target determines how aggressively you sell winners.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: No single stock should hold your portfolio hostage — cap the concentration
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: When a stock rallies hard, it can grow from 10% of your portfolio to 25%+ without you adding a share. That concentration means a single stock's reversal can drag down your entire season. This rule automatically trims oversized positions back to a target weight. The gap between max and target is the key lever: a narrow gap (15% max, 13% target) triggers frequent small trims, while a wide gap (25% max, 15% target) allows positions to grow significantly before a larger trim. Pairs naturally with Add to Winners — together they create a "pyramid up to the cap" strategy.

forgeTemplates.text: Trim any position above {maxPct}% back to {targetPct}%

maxPct.label: Max Weight
maxPct.hint: When a position hits this weight, trimming begins.

targetPct.label: Target Weight
targetPct.hint: Trim down to this weight. Smaller gap = more frequent trims.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Trims positions exceeding the max weight back to the target weight. Hard priority. Prevents single-stock concentration.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Cash Deployment Trigger
forgeRuleTemplates.description: If cash builds up past a threshold, prioritize finding new entries. Prevents accidentally becoming a cash-heavy portfolio after exits.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: Cash earns zero in a 4-week sprint — deploy it or lose the race
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: After exits fire — stop-losses, profit targets, earnings exits — cash accumulates. In a 4-week season, idle cash is a direct drag on returns. This rule monitors your cash percentage and triggers entry scans when it exceeds the threshold. It also serves a dual role on Day 1: the cron reads this threshold to determine how much cash to reserve during initial portfolio construction. A low threshold (5-10%) keeps you nearly fully invested at all times, while a higher threshold (30-40%) maintains a war chest for opportunistic entries.

forgeTemplates.text: If cash exceeds {pct}%, prioritize deploying into entry candidates

pct.label: Cash Threshold
pct.hint: Low (5-10%) = stay fully invested. High (30-40%) = big cash buffer is OK.

forgeRuleTemplates.agentUseDescription: Triggers entry scan when cash exceeds the threshold. Soft priority. Also determines initial cash reserve on Day 1 portfolio construction.

forgeRuleTemplates.headline: Sector Drift Rebalance
forgeRuleTemplates.description: If market moves push one sector too far from your starting allocation, rebalance back. Strategic asset allocation vs. letting the market decide.
forgeRuleTemplates.hook: Markets will drift your portfolio into concentration — this rule fights back
forgeRuleTemplates.learnMore: Even a well-diversified portfolio drifts over time as different sectors perform differently. If tech rallies 15% while energy drops 10%, your originally balanced allocation becomes tech-heavy. This rule compares each sector's current weight to its initial weight and triggers rebalancing when the drift exceeds the tolerance. Tight tolerance (5%) maintains strict strategic allocation, while loose tolerance (20%) lets market momentum run before correcting. This is the season-mode equivalent of institutional strategic asset allocation.

forgeTemplates.text: If any sector drifts more than {tolerance}% from initial weight, rebalance
